verdict.evidence_span_b: het verbod om bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens en persoonsgegevens van strafrechtelijke aard te verwerken door een commissie of adviescollege als bedoeld in het eerste lid niet van toepassing indien:

verdict.shared_actor: A controller or processor processing personal data, potentially including a controller or processor not established in the Union
verdict.shared_circumstance: Processing personal data in circumstances where the GDPR rules may apply; however, Norm B concerns an exception to the obligation to appoint an EU representative, while Norm A concerns processing special categories of personal data
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A prohibits processing personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade-union membership, and processing genetic, biometric-for-unique-identification, health, sexual-behaviour, or sexual-orientation data, subject to the GDPR's exceptions referenced in Article 9.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B provides that the obligation in Article 27(1) does not apply to certain occasional, low-risk processing that does not involve large-scale processing of special-category data or criminal-conviction/offence data, or to a public authority or body.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Norm B does not authorize the prohibited processing described in Norm A; it only removes an EU-representative obligation in specified cases. Whether a particular processing operation is lawful under an exception to Article 9(1), as referenced by Norm A, is not specified in the supplied text.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different duties on different legal objects: Norm A regulates whether certain processing may occur, whereas Norm B regulates whether an Article 27(1) representative-appointment obligation applies. Compliance with the representative exception does not require the prohibited processing, and the processing prohibition does not require appointment of a representative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Overeenkomstig artikel 9, eerste lid, van de verordening zijn verwerking van persoonsgegevens waaruit ras of etnische afkomst, politieke opvattingen, religieuze of levensbeschouwelijke overtuigingen, of het lidmaatschap van een vakbond blijken, en verwerking van genetische gegevens, biometrische gegevens met het oog op de unieke identificatie van een persoon, of gegevens over gezondheid, of gegevens met betrekking tot iemands seksueel gedrag of seksuele gerichtheid verboden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verplichting vervat in lid 1 van dit artikel geldt niet voor: a) incidentele verwerking die geen grootschalige verwerking van bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, betreft noch verwerking van persoonsgegevens die verband houden met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10, en waarbij de kans gering is dat zij een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen, rekening houdend met de aard, de context, de omvang en de verwerkingsdoeleinden; of b) een overheidsinstantie of overheidsorgaan.

verdict.shared_actor: An organization or undertaking processing personal data, potentially including one with fewer than 250 employees
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes special categories of personal data as described in Article 9(1), including health, biometric, genetic, or similar sensitive data. Norm B concerns whether the record-of-processing-activities obligations apply; Norm A concerns whether such processing is prohibited.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A prohibits processing personal data revealing the listed sensitive characteristics and other Article 9(1) special-category data, subject to the exceptions in the GDPR (as referenced by the provision).
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B provides that the obligations in Article 30(1) and (2) do not apply to organizations with fewer than 250 employees unless, among other circumstances, the processing concerns special categories of data under Article 9(1). It therefore concerns an exception to the record-keeping obligation, not a prohibition on processing.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Norm A expressly refers to the exceptions in the GDPR, but the supplied text does not identify which Article 9(2) exception might permit the processing. Norm B does not resolve the legality of the processing; it only determines whether the Article 30 record-keeping exception applies. The interaction with the other Article 30 conditions is also not necessary to establish a contradiction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms address different duties: Norm A prohibits certain processing, while Norm B removes an exemption from record-keeping obligations when special-category processing occurs. They do not impose mutually exclusive requirements on the same actor for the same trigger, and both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Overeenkomstig artikel 9, eerste lid, van de verordening zijn verwerking van persoonsgegevens waaruit ras of etnische afkomst, politieke opvattingen, religieuze of levensbeschouwelijke overtuigingen, of het lidmaatschap van een vakbond blijken, en verwerking van genetische gegevens, biometrische gegevens met het oog op de unieke identificatie van een persoon, of gegevens over gezondheid, of gegevens met betrekking tot iemands seksueel gedrag of seksuele gerichtheid verboden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben, tenzij het waarschijnlijk is dat de verwerking die zij verrichten een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkenen, de verwerking niet incidenteel is, of de verwerking bijzondere categorieën van gegevens, als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, of persoonsgegevens in verband met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10 betreft.

verdict.shared_actor: Any person or organization processing personal data, potentially including a controller or processor subject to BWBR0040940
verdict.shared_circumstance: Processing personal data that reveals racial or ethnic origin and also involves a legally prescribed national identification number, where the processing is for identification or another purpose permitted by law
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A generally prohibits processing personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, but makes that prohibition inapplicable when the stated identification or affirmative-action conditions are satisfied.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B permits use of a legally prescribed number for identifying a person only to execute the relevant law or for purposes determined by law.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a particular processing operation involving both racial/ethnic-origin data and a national identification number is authorized by the relevant law or falls within one of Norm A's exceptions. That factual and legal authorization remains unresolved.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms regulate different aspects of the same possible processing operation: Norm A concerns when processing racial/ethnic-origin data is exempted from a prohibition, while Norm B limits the purposes for which a national identification number may be used. Norm B does not require use of such a number, and Norm A does not require processing it. Both can therefore be complied with by processing only where Norm A's conditions are met and using the number only for a legally authorized purpose.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verbod om persoonsgegevens te verwerken waaruit ras of etnische afkomst blijkt, niet van toepassing, indien de verwerking geschiedt:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een nummer dat ter identificatie van een persoon bij wet is voorgeschreven, wordt bij de verwerking van persoonsgegevens slechts gebruikt ter uitvoering van de desbetreffende wet dan wel voor doeleinden bij de wet bepaald.

verdict.shared_actor: A controller or decision-maker processing personal data and making a decision covered by Article 22(2), potentially involving data revealing racial or ethnic origin.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes or uses personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin in connection with an Article 22(2) automated individual decision, where Article 9(2)(g) may provide a legal basis.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A creates an exception to the prohibition on processing data revealing racial or ethnic origin when the processing is unavoidable for identification, or is necessary for specified affirmative-action purposes and satisfies the listed data, statutory-criteria, and written-objection conditions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits basing an Article 22(2) decision on Article 9(1) special-category data, unless Article 9(2)(a) or (g) applies and appropriate measures protect the data subject’s legitimate interests.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved on the supplied text whether the particular processing satisfies all conditions of Article 25 and whether the required appropriate protective measures under Article 22 are in place. Norm A permits certain processing; it does not itself require that an automated decision be based on the data, while Norm B separately permits such reliance only when its additional safeguards are met.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms are jointly satisfiable: Article 25’s Article 9(2)(g) exception can coexist with Article 22’s conditional exception. Norm B does not forbid all use of the data; it prohibits reliance on it for covered decisions only absent the stated legal basis and safeguards. No mutually exclusive duties are imposed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verbod om persoonsgegevens te verwerken waaruit ras of etnische afkomst blijkt, niet van toepassing, indien de verwerking geschiedt:
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 2 bedoelde besluiten worden niet gebaseerd op de in artikel 9, lid 1, bedoelde bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens, tenzij artikel 9, lid 2, punt a) of g), van toepassing is en er passende maatregelen ter bescherming van de gerechtvaardigde belangen van de betrokkene zijn getroffen.

verdict.shared_actor: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of andere actor die persoonsgegevens verwerkt en onder de voorwaarden van beide bepalingen valt.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Een verwerking van persoonsgegevens waarvoor Norm A een uitzondering op het verbod wegens ras of etnische afkomst kan bieden, en die tevens verwerking is uit hoofde van artikel 6, lid 1, onder c of e AVG met een reeds uitgevoerde algemene gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A bepaalt dat het verbod op verwerking van persoonsgegevens waaruit ras of etnische afkomst blijkt niet van toepassing is wanneer de verwerking voor identificatie onvermijdelijk is, of — onder de daar genoemde voorwaarden — noodzakelijk is voor het toekennen van een bevoorrechte positie aan een bepaalde etnische of culturele minderheidsgroep.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B bepaalt dat de leden 1 tot en met 7 van artikel 35 niet van toepassing zijn wanneer de specifieke verwerking al is geregeld in de rechtsgrond en er in het kader van de vaststelling daarvan al een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling is uitgevoerd, tenzij de lidstaten voorafgaande beoordeling noodzakelijk achten.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Het blijft onduidelijk of de lidstaat in de concrete situatie een voorafgaande gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling noodzakelijk acht. Ook moet afzonderlijk worden voldaan aan de voorwaarden van Norm A; Norm B regelt alleen de toepasselijkheid van bepaalde effectbeoordelingsverplichtingen en verbiedt de verwerking niet.
verdict.criterion_fired: De bepalingen leggen geen onderling onverenigbare verplichtingen op. Norm A bevat een uitzondering op een verwerkingsverbod onder specifieke voorwaarden, terwijl Norm B onder voorwaarden bepaalde effectbeoordelingsverplichtingen buiten toepassing laat. Beide kunnen gelijktijdig worden nageleefd; de uitzondering in Norm B voor een door de lidstaat noodzakelijk geachte voorafgaande beoordeling voorkomt bovendien geen gezamenlijke naleving.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verbod om persoonsgegevens te verwerken waaruit ras of etnische afkomst blijkt, niet van toepassing, indien de verwerking geschiedt:
verdict.evidence_span_b: zijn de leden 1 tot en met 7 niet van toepassing, tenzij de lidstaten het noodzakelijk achten om voorafgaand aan de verwerkingen een dergelijke beoordeling uit te voeren.

verdict.shared_actor: A provider/processor handling personal data in the context described by Norm A and subject to the notification duty in Norm B
verdict.shared_circumstance: Personal data are involved and a personal-data breach is likely to have adverse consequences for the data subject's privacy; Norm A additionally requires that the data concern religious or philosophical beliefs and are processed for spiritual care, while disclosure to a third party occurs without the data subject's consent.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A prohibits providing personal data to third parties without the data subject's consent.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the provider to notify the person concerned without delay of a personal-data breach when the breach is likely to have adverse consequences for that person's privacy.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether notifying the data subject under Norm B is itself a disclosure to a third party under Norm A, nor do they clarify how the notification duty applies if the breach involved disclosure without consent. On the texts provided, notification can plausibly be made to the data subject rather than to a third party, so no contradiction is established.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose different duties concerning different recipients and actions: Norm A restricts disclosure to third parties, whereas Norm B requires notification to the data subject. They are not mutually exclusive, and the texts provide a plausible route to comply with both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In de gevallen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, worden geen persoonsgegevens aan derden verstrekt zonder toestemming van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_actor: A controller or other party disclosing personal data to third parties in the context of spiritual care, and B a public-law-established legal person (or a party acting on its behalf) providing an information-society service; overlap is possible only if the same actor performs both roles.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap where personal data are disclosed to third parties without the data subject's consent while a user is accessing an information-society service provided by or on behalf of a public-law-established legal person.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A prohibits providing personal data to third parties without the data subject's consent in the specified spiritual-care cases.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits making a user's access to the information-society service conditional on granting consent referred to in the first paragraph.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish that Norm A's consent for disclosure is the same consent as Norm B's consent for access, nor that access is being conditioned on disclosure consent. The provisions may therefore apply to different acts or consents; the precise scope of the reference to 'het eerste lid' is also not supplied.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction is shown: Norm A requires consent before a specified disclosure, while Norm B forbids conditioning service access on granting a specified consent. Both can be complied with by obtaining consent without making access conditional on it, or by not disclosing the data.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In de gevallen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, worden geen persoonsgegevens aan derden verstrekt zonder toestemming van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_actor: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of andere actor die persoonsgegevens aan derden verstrekt en tevens verantwoordelijk is voor een verwerking die op toestemming berust.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Een verwerking van persoonsgegevens, mogelijk met verstrekking aan derden, waarbij toestemming van de betrokkene relevant is of wordt aangevoerd als grondslag.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A verbiedt het verstrekken van persoonsgegevens aan derden zonder toestemming van de betrokkene.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, wanneer de verwerking op toestemming berust, te kunnen aantonen dat de betrokkene toestemming heeft gegeven voor de verwerking van diens persoonsgegevens.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Niet vastgesteld is of de toestemming voor de verwerking onder Norm B ook specifiek en rechtsgeldig de verstrekking aan derden dekt, zoals Norm A vereist. De bepalingen geven evenmin uitsluitsel over situaties waarin toestemming ontbreekt of niet kan worden aangetoond.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichtingen zijn verenigbaar: Norm A vereist toestemming vóór verstrekking aan derden, terwijl Norm B bewijs van gegeven toestemming vereist wanneer de verwerking op toestemming berust. De ene norm verbiedt niet wat de andere verplicht; de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kan beide naleven door alleen met toestemming te verstrekken en die toestemming te kunnen aantonen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In de gevallen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, worden geen persoonsgegevens aan derden verstrekt zonder toestemming van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de verwerking berust op toestemming, moet de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kunnen aantonen dat de betrokkene toestemming heeft gegeven voor de verwerking van zijn persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_actor: The entity processing or disclosing the data (the controller or other responsible data-processing actor)
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor is handling personal data in a situation covered by Norm A and the data subject has objected to processing for direct marketing under Norm B. The texts do not establish that these circumstances necessarily coincide.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A prohibits providing personal data to third parties without the data subject’s consent, in the cases referred to in its first paragraph.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits further processing the personal data for direct-marketing purposes when the data subject objects to such processing.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular disclosure to a third party would also constitute processing for direct-marketing purposes, and whether the disclosure is covered by Norm A’s referenced first-paragraph cases. If both apply, the actor can comply with both by obtaining consent before disclosure and ceasing direct-marketing processing after an objection; the provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms regulate different acts: Norm A concerns disclosure to third parties without consent, while Norm B concerns continued processing for direct marketing after an objection. No provision requires an act that the other forbids, and simultaneous compliance is possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In de gevallen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, worden geen persoonsgegevens aan derden verstrekt zonder toestemming van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de betrokkene bezwaar maakt tegen verwerking ten behoeve van direct marketing, worden de persoonsgegevens niet meer voor deze doeleinden verwerkt.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent Dutch public rule-making authorities (the government acting by algemene maatregel van bestuur under Article 30, and the Minister of Health, Welfare and Sport acting by ministerial regulation under Article 30a); the provisions do not establish that exactly the same authority must act.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern making further rules about the application of specified paragraphs concerning exceptions involving health data or health-data dossier transfers. The texts do not establish identical subject matter or an exclusive allocation of regulatory authority.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 30 authorizes further rules to be made by algemene maatregel van bestuur concerning the application of the first paragraph and the third paragraph, opening words and point b.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 30a authorizes further rules to be made by regulation of the Minister of Health, Welfare and Sport concerning the application of the first, second, or third paragraph.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It remains unresolved whether other statutory provisions allocate the same regulatory subject matter exclusively to one instrument or authority, or otherwise limit overlap. On the supplied text alone, both competences can coexist; neither provision requires an act that the other forbids.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction: both are permissive competences to issue further rules, and the provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties or prohibit the exercise authorized by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij regeling van Onze Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld over de toepassing van het eerste, tweede of derde lid.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent public authorities under the statute, potentially including the executive authority empowered to issue an algemene maatregel van bestuur and the named Ministers; the texts do not establish that the same specific actor must perform both acts.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the operation of BWBR0040940, but no specific common triggering circumstance is stated: Article 30 concerns rules on applying its first paragraph and third paragraph, opening clause and point b, while Article 48a concerns the entry into force of Article 48a and specified assets.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 30 grants a competence: rules concerning the application of the specified provisions may be laid down by algemene maatregel van bestuur.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 48a requires that the assets referred to in its fourth paragraph transfer at the time of entry into force at a value to be determined by Our Minister in agreement with Our Minister of Finance.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether the same authority, procedure, or factual transaction is involved, nor do they address any interaction between the delegated rule-making competence and the valuation determination. The supplied text therefore does not establish a direct overlap beyond the broad statutory context.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction is shown: neither provision requires an act that the other forbids, and their stated subject matters and triggers are distinct. The duties/competence can be exercised concurrently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in het vierde lid bedoelde vermogensbestanddelen gaan op het tijdstip van inwerkingtreding van dit artikel onder algemene titel over op tegen een door Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister van Financiën te bepalen waarde.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent public authority empowered to issue or determine matters by algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern regulation or determination by AMvB, but they address different subject matters; the text does not establish that the same AMvB, authority, or factual trigger must be involved.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence to lay down further rules concerning the application of the first and third paragraphs, opening sentence and point b, of Article 30.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B provides that an AMvB determines the functional scope of an appointed standard, the bodies subject to the obligation to apply it, and the date that obligation begins.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify the competent authority, procedural limits, or whether rules made under Norm A could overlap with determinations under Norm B. Any such overlap cannot be inferred to create mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both are compatible AMvB competences concerning distinct regulatory subjects; neither requires the authority to do something the other forbids, and the text does not establish mutually exclusive duties for the same trigger.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b:
Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur wordt bepaald:

a.
het functionele toepassingsbereik van een aangewezen standaard,

b.
de organen waarvoor de verplichting tot toepassing van een aangewezen standaard geldt, en

c.
de datum waarop de verplichting tot toepassing van een aangewezen standaard ingaat.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent public authority empowered to issue rules by algemene maatregel van bestuur (not necessarily the same authority, and the text does not identify it more specifically)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the possible making of further rules by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur; however, they address different subject matters.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A authorizes further rules concerning the application of the first paragraph and the third paragraph, opening words and point b, of Article 30, regarding health data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes rules concerning the disclosure/access and cooperation referred to in its third paragraph, and cooperation between recognized services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify the competent rule-making authority, the relationship between any implementing regulations, or whether their subject matters could overlap in a particular case. Nothing in the text indicates mutually exclusive rule-making powers.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both norms confer compatible rule-making competences over different subject matters. Neither requires an act that the other forbids, and both competences can be exercised simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent authority empowered to issue a algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB), presumably the executive/regulatory authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the possible adoption of rules by AMvB, but they address different subject matters: application of specified provisions concerning health data in Norm A, and payment-method choices for supplied electronic communications services in Norm B.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence to establish further rules concerning the application of Article 30(1) and Article 30(3)(b).
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B grants competence to establish rules concerning the available choices for the method of payment for supplied electronic communications services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify the scope, content, or interaction of any AMvB adopted under either competence. Any overlap in a concrete implementing measure would require separate analysis, but no mutually exclusive duty or prohibition appears in these texts.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both norms confer permissive rule-making competences in distinct subject areas; neither requires or prohibits conduct that the other requires or prohibits. The competences can be exercised simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen regels worden gesteld ten aanzien van de keuzemogelijkheden voor de wijze van betaling van geleverde elektronische communicatiediensten.

verdict.shared_actor: The authority empowered to issue general administrative orders (algemene maatregel van bestuur), with Norm B additionally requiring agreement with the Minister of Security and Justice.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the making of further rules by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur in relation to specified underlying statutory requirements, exceptions, or provisions.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence to establish further rules concerning the application of the first paragraph and the third paragraph, opening words and point b, of its provision.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B grants competence to give further rules concerning the requirements in the first paragraph, under a and b, and the exceptions in the third paragraph, provided this is done in agreement with the Minister of Security and Justice.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions may concern overlapping subject matter, but the supplied text does not establish that they regulate the same underlying requirements or that either authority is prohibited from exercising its competence. The precise scope and any coordination between the two rule-making powers remain unresolved.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms confer potentially overlapping rule-making competences, but neither requires conduct that the other forbids or imposes mutually exclusive duties. The text is insufficient to determine whether the competences are legally concurrent, hierarchically coordinated, or otherwise limited.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen in overeenstemming met Onze Minister van Veiligheid en Justitie nadere regels worden gegeven met betrekking tot de in het eerste lid, onder a en b, genoemde vereisten en de in het derde lid genoemde uitzonderingen.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent authority empowered to issue a algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the possible making of further rules by AMvB, but they address different underlying statutory subject matters.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A authorizes further rules concerning the application of the first paragraph and the third paragraph, opening words and point b, of Article 30.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes further rules concerning the investigation, data provision, cooperation obligation, and notification of data provision referred to in Article 11.11, paragraphs four through six.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether the underlying subject matters overlap or whether another legal rule limits the exercise of either competence. No textual priority or exclusive allocation of rule-making power is provided.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both norms confer permissive, potentially cumulative competence to make further rules; neither requires conduct that the other forbids, and joint exercise is plausibly possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen omtrent de toepassing van het eerste lid en het derde lid, aanhef en onderdeel b, nadere regels worden gesteld.

verdict.shared_actor: A person responsible for processing personal data who is also a member of, or acts for, a temporary committee or advisory body under Article 47a
verdict.shared_circumstance: Processing special-category personal data (including health data) or criminal-law personal data in the Article 47a circumstances: necessary for a task of substantial public interest, consent is impossible or disproportionately burdensome, and appropriate safeguards are provided.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 30, where the relevant exception applies, the controller who personally processes the data must keep the data confidential, unless the law requires disclosure or the controller's task necessitates disclosure to others who are authorized to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 47a states that the prohibition on a committee or advisory body processing special-category or criminal-law personal data does not apply when the listed public-interest, consent, and safeguard conditions are met; it therefore permits such processing subject to those conditions.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify all operational limits of disclosure under Article 30 or how the Article 47a safeguards interact with a particular confidentiality obligation. However, Article 30 itself permits disclosure where legally required or necessary to the controller's task and to persons authorized to process the data.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose compatible requirements: Article 47a removes a processing prohibition under specified conditions, while Article 30 imposes confidentiality on the person processing the data, subject to stated disclosure exceptions. Nothing in Article 47a requires disclosure or forbids confidentiality, so joint compliance is possible.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller who is also a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie subject to Norm B, and who processes the health data covered by Norm A.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes health data under one of the situations referred to in Article 30(1), (2), or (3), while also being required to submit the auditor's declaration to the Minister.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller to keep the health data confidential, unless the law requires disclosure or the controller's task makes disclosure necessary to others who are authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3) to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires bestuursorganen and aangewezen organisaties to submit to the Minister an auditor's declaration showing whether they comply with the rules referred to in Article 4(1).
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can submit the auditor's declaration without disclosing the underlying health data—for example, by providing a declaration limited to the auditor's compliance conclusion, using anonymised or aggregated information, or restricting any disclosure to persons legally authorized to process the data. The text does not state that the declaration must contain confidential health data.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether, in a particular case, the auditor's declaration or the audit process requires identifiable health data to be disclosed to the Minister or another auditor, and whether that recipient is authorized under Norm A or disclosure is otherwise legally required or necessary for the controller's task.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A provision requiring the actor to include identifiable health data in the declaration and prohibiting anonymisation or restricted disclosure, without making the recipient legally authorized or the disclosure legally required, could make joint compliance impossible. Conversely, an explicit authorization or disclosure requirement would reinforce joint compliance.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different duties and the text supports a plausible compliant method of satisfying both; neither provision requires what the other forbids.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties overleggen aan Onze Minister een verklaring van een auditor waaruit blijkt of zij voldoen aan de in het eerste lid bedoelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a verwerkingsverantwoordelijke who is also a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie; the texts do not establish that these categories overlap in every case.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The same processing or electronic-service context could involve both rules if the actor processes health data under Article 30 and is subject to the electronic-access security rules under Article 4.
verdict.requirement_a: Under the stated conditions, the controller must keep the health data confidential, subject to disclosure where the law requires it or where the controller's task makes disclosure necessary to others who are authorised to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Administrative bodies and designated organisations must comply with rules established by or under a general administrative measure concerning the operation, reliability, and security of access to electronic services at different reliability levels.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can maintain confidentiality while complying with access-security rules by restricting electronic access to authorised persons, using appropriate authentication and reliability levels, and disclosing data only where Article 30 permits or requires it. The security obligation does not on its face require unrestricted disclosure of the health data.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The precise implementing rules under the general administrative measure, the actor's exact status, and whether a particular security measure would require disclosure to an unauthorised person are not provided. Article 30's task-based necessity exception also requires factual assessment.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A specific implementing security rule requiring the same actor to disclose the protected health data to a person or class of persons whom Article 30 forbids it to disclose to, without a lawful exception or compliant restricted-access alternative, could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Facts showing that the actor is not subject to both provisions would instead eliminate the overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, facially compatible duties: confidentiality of health data and compliance with electronic-access security rules. Neither text requires what the other forbids, and restricted authorised access provides a plausible joint-compliance route.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties voldoen aan bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur te stellen regels met betrekking tot de werking, betrouwbaarheid en beveiliging van de toegang tot elektronische diensten op verschillende betrouwbaarheidsniveaus.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller or other person processing health data under Norm A, and a public body or designated organisation using a public identification means or the facility under Norm B, but the provisions do not clearly establish that the same actor must be both.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Only potentially where the same public body or designated organisation processes health data while using a public identification means or facility for electronic public services. The texts do not expressly state that this overlap occurs.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, where no pre-existing confidentiality duty applies, to keep the health data confidential, subject to disclosure required by law or necessary for the controller's task to other persons authorised to process the data under the specified provisions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B restricts use of a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility exclusively to access to electronic services provided by administrative bodies and designated organisations.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Use the identification means solely to authenticate or provide access to the defined electronic public service, while keeping any health data confidential and disclosing it only where legally required or necessary to authorised processors. Access controls, limited disclosure, and anonymisation or minimisation where feasible would satisfy both rules.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not resolve whether a particular health-data disclosure is legally required or necessary for the controller's task, nor whether the contemplated use of the identification means is in fact access to the defined electronic service. Norm A's statutory/task-based disclosure exceptions remain applicable.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that compliance with the electronic service necessarily requires a disclosure of health data that Norm A absolutely forbids, or that Norm B requires use of the identification means for a non-service purpose that Norm B prohibits, could change the assessment. The specific identity and legal capacities of the actor and the purpose of the proposed use would also matter.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms regulate different conduct and contain no mutually exclusive duties: confidentiality under Norm A can coexist with the purpose limitation on identification means under Norm B. The provisions do not establish a shared trigger requiring one rule's prohibited conduct to perform the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, worden uitsluitend gebruikt voor de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening door bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an erkende ontsluitende dienst that is also the verwerkingsverantwoordelijke processing health data, or acts through such a responsible party.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The circumstances overlap only if the recognized unlocking service must disclose recognized business/organizational means, authorization statements, or designated attributes in electronic public-service access, and those materials contain health data processed by the same actor under the conditions of Article 30.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the responsible party to keep the health data confidential, unless the law requires disclosure or the party's task makes disclosure necessary to others who are authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3) to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires an erkende ontsluitende dienst to unlock all recognized business and organizational means, all relevant electronic authorization statements, and all attributes designated under Article 12.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The service can comply with Norm B while limiting disclosure to the required recipient, data, and access context, using authorization and access controls and excluding or protecting health data where it is not among the required attributes. Norm A itself permits disclosure where legally required or necessary for the task to persons authorized to process the data.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not establish whether the materials that must be unlocked under Norm B contain health data, whether Norm B requires disclosure of such data to persons not authorized under Norm A, or whether another provision requires or limits disclosure. It also does not establish that the erkende ontsluitende dienst is the Article 30 verwerkingsverantwoordelijke.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if Norm B, in the same circumstances, expressly required disclosure of health data to a recipient who is not authorized under Article 30 and no Article 30 exception or other legal duty permitted that disclosure; conversely, proof that the relevant data contain no health data would remove the apparent overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not, on the supplied text, establish mutually exclusive duties. Joint compliance appears plausible, but the factual overlap and recipient authorization needed for a firm NOT_A_CONFLICT determination are not shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien toepassing wordt gegeven aan het eerste, tweede of derde lid, worden de gegevens alleen verwerkt door personen die uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift dan wel krachtens een overeenkomst tot geheimhouding zijn verplicht. Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een erkende ontsluitende dienst ontsluit alle erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen, alle door erkende machtigingsdiensten afgegeven elektronische verklaringen waaruit blijkt dat een natuurlijke persoon, onderneming of rechtspersoon gemachtigd is namens de onderneming of rechtspersoon, bedoeld in artikel 15, eerste lid, op te treden bij de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening en alle op grond van artikel 12 aangewezen attributen.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the verwerkingsverantwoordelijke under Norm A if it is also an erkende middelenuitgever, erkende authenticatiedienst, or erkende machtigingsdienst under Norm B.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes health data under one of the situations referred to in Article 30(1), (2), or (3), while also being required to cooperate with an erkende ontsluitende dienst for the proper unlocking of an erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, where it is not already subject to a professional, official, or statutory confidentiality duty, to keep the health data confidential. Disclosure is permitted where the law requires communication or where the controller's task makes communication necessary to others authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3) to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires an erkende middelenuitgever, erkende authenticatiedienst, or erkende machtigingsdienst to provide an erkende ontsluitende dienst with all cooperation necessary for proper unlocking of an erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel and reliable access to the desired electronic service, without charging costs.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can provide only the cooperation necessary for the electronic-service access, while withholding health data unless disclosure is legally required or necessary for its task to another person authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3). If health data are genuinely necessary, disclosure can be limited to the minimum necessary and made only to an authorized recipient, potentially through a restricted or otherwise safeguarded disclosure process.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish whether the cooperation required by Norm B actually entails disclosure or processing of health data, whether such data are necessary for unlocking or access, or whether the erkende ontsluitende dienst or its personnel are authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3). Norm A's statutory/task-necessity exceptions may therefore determine the result in a concrete case.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if Norm B is interpreted to require this same actor to disclose specific health data to a recipient who is not authorized under Article 30(1), (2), or (3), and no law independently requires or permits that disclosure. Conversely, proof that no health data are involved, or that the recipient is authorized and the disclosure is necessary for the actor's task, would confirm joint compliance.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same established trigger. Norm A itself permits disclosure where legally required or necessary to communicate with an authorized processor, while Norm B requires necessary cooperation but does not expressly require disclosure of health data to an unauthorized recipient. The available text therefore supports a compliant, limited-cooperation alternative rather than a contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een erkende middelenuitgever, erkende authenticatiedienst en erkende machtigingsdienst verlenen aan een erkende ontsluitende dienst alle benodigde medewerking die voor een goede ontsluiting van een erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel en een betrouwbare toegang tot de gewenste elektronische dienstverlening noodzakelijk is.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller or other person processing health data under Norm A who is also a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie operating its own electronic service under Norm B.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The shared actor processes health data under one of the situations referred to in Article 30(1)–(3), while an incident involving the security or integrity of its own electronic service, or misuse/improper use of access to that service, occurs. The texts do not expressly establish that every such incident involves health data.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, if not already subject to a professional, official, or statutory confidentiality duty, to keep the data confidential. This is subject to exceptions where the law requires disclosure or the controller’s task makes disclosure necessary to others authorized under Article 30(1)–(3) to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify the Minister of the Interior and Kingdom Relations without delay of a security or integrity breach of its own electronic service, or misuse/improper use of access to that service, and to provide all necessary information.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Yes. The actor can make the required notification while limiting the disclosure to information necessary for the incident report, using anonymisation, pseudonymisation, aggregation, or other safeguards where feasible, and disclosing identifiable health data only to the extent that Norm B or another applicable law requires it. Norm A itself permits disclosure where the law requires it or where the actor’s task makes disclosure necessary to authorized recipients; the provisions do not state that the Minister is unauthorized to receive incident information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether Norm B’s phrase “alle benodigde informatie” in a particular case requires identifiable health data, whether the Minister or recipients are subject to an adequate confidentiality basis, and whether another applicable secrecy or data-protection rule restricts the disclosure. The provisions supplied do not expressly reconcile the Minister’s authority with Norm A’s authorized-recipient condition.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if a concrete incident required Norm B’s notification to include identifiable health data and the law did not require or otherwise authorize that disclosure, while no anonymised, pseudonymised, aggregated, or other sufficient report could satisfy Norm B. It could also change if the Minister were legally prohibited from receiving the relevant data.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not mutually exclusive on the supplied text: confidentiality under Norm A contains disclosure exceptions, and Norm B requires incident reporting. A restricted or de-identified report, or legally required disclosure of only necessary information, can plausibly satisfy both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening. Het bestuursorgaan of de aangewezen organisatie verstrekt daarbij alle benodigde informatie.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller or other person processing health data who also falls within Norm B’s listed entities (a bestuursorgaan, aangewezen organisatie, qualifying recognition holder, or recognised means issuer/service provider).
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes health data under the circumstances referred to in Norm A and is requested or independently needs to provide data or information to the Minister for measures concerning prevention or termination of interference with secure and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, where no pre-existing professional, statutory, or official secrecy duty applies, to keep the health data confidential, subject to disclosure where the law requires it or where the controller’s task makes disclosure necessary to others authorised under the referenced provisions to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the listed entities, on request and on their own initiative, to provide the Minister with the data and information he needs to take measures to prevent or end interference with secure and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can disclose only the data and information actually needed by the Minister, using a legally authorised and appropriately limited disclosure. Norm A expressly permits disclosure where the law requires it or where the actor’s task makes it necessary to disclose to persons authorised to process the data. If the Minister is not an authorised recipient under Norm A, the parties could use anonymised or otherwise non-identifying information, or establish a lawful disclosure route and limit the disclosure to the necessary information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not establish whether Norm B legally requires disclosure of identifiable health data, whether the Minister is a person authorised under Norm A to process those data, or whether another statutory secrecy exception applies. It also does not specify whether the information needed under Norm B can be supplied in anonymised or aggregated form.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if Norm B is shown to require disclosure of identifiable health data in a case where the Minister is not legally authorised to receive or process them and no exception in Norm A or other law permits disclosure. Conversely, confirmation that the Minister is an authorised recipient or that anonymised information suffices would reinforce the non-conflict finding.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose potentially overlapping duties, but they are not mutually exclusive on the text provided. Norm A contains express exceptions for legally required or task-necessary disclosure, and Norm B does not expressly require disclosure in a form that necessarily violates the confidentiality duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller or other person processing health data who is also responsible for ensuring authorised personnel access to personal data.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both rules may apply when health-related personal data are processed and access or disclosure to personnel is being arranged for a legally permitted purpose.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, where not already subject to a professional, statutory, or official secrecy duty, to keep the data confidential, subject to disclosure required by law or necessary for the controller’s task to others authorised under the referenced provisions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires measures ensuring that only authorised personnel have access to personal data for legally permitted purposes, and also requires protection against unauthorised access or disclosure.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Limit access and any disclosure to personnel who are legally authorised and bound by confidentiality, and implement access controls so that only such personnel can access the data for legally permitted purposes. Norm A’s express exceptions also permit disclosures required by law or necessary for the controller’s task to authorised recipients.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The precise scope of the authorisation under Norm B and whether a particular disclosure is legally required or necessary for the controller’s task under Norm A are not specified. Those issues may affect whether a particular access event is permitted, but the provisions do not inherently require incompatible conduct.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could arise only if a specific fact showed that Norm A required disclosure to a person or category of persons whom Norm B prohibited from accessing the data, or that Norm B required access to a person whom Norm A absolutely prohibited from receiving it, with no applicable exception or compliant restricted-access arrangement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are compatible: confidentiality and protection against unauthorised access can be satisfied by restricting access to legally authorised, confidentiality-bound personnel. Norm A expressly accommodates legally required or task-necessary disclosure to authorised recipients.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller/personally processing controller under Norm A and a provider subject to the notification duty under Norm B, potentially where the same organisation has both roles.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both could concern the handling of personal or health-related data and protective measures, but the provisions do not establish the same trigger or clearly apply to the same legal situation.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller, if not already bound by professional, official or statutory confidentiality, to keep the data confidential, subject to disclosure where the law requires it or the controller's task makes disclosure necessary to persons authorised to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B provides that the notification referred to in its second paragraph is not required when, in the opinion of the Dutch Data Protection Authority, appropriate technical protective measures make the relevant personal data encrypted or otherwise unintelligible to anyone without access rights.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can maintain confidentiality under Norm A while using appropriate encryption or other technical measures and, if the Authority considers those measures sufficient, rely on Norm B's exception so that the notification is not required. If the exception is unavailable, confidentiality and the notification duty could still ordinarily be performed together.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the same actor is subject to both provisions, whether Norm A's health-data conditions are met, whether Norm B's underlying notification duty is triggered, and whether the Authority would judge the technical measures appropriate and the data unintelligible to unauthorised persons.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contrary result would require facts or text showing that Norm B's notification necessarily entails disclosure prohibited by Norm A, or that the notification duty and the confidentiality duty are triggered for the same actor and event in mutually exclusive ways. The Authority's refusal to accept the protective measures would remove Norm B's exception but would not by itself create a contradiction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties: Norm A expressly permits legally required or task-necessary disclosure to authorised processors, while Norm B concerns when a notification is not required based on technical protection. Joint compliance is therefore possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller or other person processing health data, potentially also an actor causing information to be stored on or accessed from an end-user device by means other than an electronic communications network.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both could potentially concern the same activity only if the actor and facts fall within Norm A's health-data processing provisions and Norm B's extended requirements for storing or accessing information on an end-user device by a non-network method. The texts do not establish that overlap.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires confidentiality of the health data where the controller personally processes it and is not already subject to a professional, statutory, or office-based confidentiality duty, subject to disclosure required by law or necessary for the controller's task to others authorized to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B provides that the requirements in Article 11.7(1)(a) and (b) also apply when storage of information on, or access to information stored on, an end-user device is achieved by a means other than an electronic communications network.
verdict.compliant_alternative: No conflict is apparent: the actor could comply with Norm B's applicable Article 11.7(1)(a) and (b) requirements while maintaining Norm A confidentiality, for example by limiting any device storage or access to what is permitted under Article 11.7(1)(a) and (b), and disclosing health data only where Norm A's statutory or task-necessity exception applies. The underlying Article 11.7 requirements are not provided, so the precise implementation cannot be specified.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text of Article 11.7(1)(a) and (b), the scope of the Article 30 first-to-third-lid conditions, and the facts establishing that the same actor and processing activity are covered by both provisions are not provided. It is therefore unresolved whether Norm B would permit or require any particular disclosure or device access that could engage Norm A's confidentiality rule.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become possible only if the missing Article 11.7(1)(a) or (b) text, as applied to the same actor and trigger, expressly required disclosure or device access that necessarily violated Norm A's confidentiality duty, with no statutory, task-necessity, consent, anonymisation, restriction, or other compliant route. Facts showing that the provisions do not apply to the same actor or activity would instead confirm no conflict.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same established trigger. Norm A regulates confidentiality and permitted disclosure; Norm B extends unspecified Article 11.7(1)(a) and (b) requirements to a different technical means. Joint compliance is plausibly possible, and no contrary requirement is shown.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De in het eerste lid, onder a en b, genoemde vereisten zijn ook van toepassing in het geval op een andere wijze dan door middel van een elektronisch communicatienetwerk wordt bewerkstelligd dat via een elektronisch communicatienetwerk informatie wordt opgeslagen of toegang wordt verleend tot op het randapparaat opgeslagen informatie.

verdict.shared_actor: A public-law-established legal person (or its responsible data controller) providing an information-society service, insofar as it processes health data and is subject to the confidentiality duty in Norm A.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor provides such a service and processes health data under one of the situations referred to in Article 30(1), (2), or (3), while access to the service is being arranged. The texts do not expressly establish that both provisions apply to the same transaction.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the responsible controller to keep the health data confidential, unless the law requires disclosure or the controller’s task makes disclosure necessary to others who are authorised to process the data.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits making a user’s access to an information-society service provided by or on behalf of a public-law-established legal person conditional on granting consent under Article 11.7(1).
verdict.compliant_alternative: Provide access without conditioning it on consent under Article 11.7(1), while separately maintaining confidentiality of the health data. If disclosure is necessary, disclose only to persons authorised under Norm A, using restricted disclosure or anonymisation where compatible with the service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the service-access arrangement would in practice require the user to grant the specific consent covered by Norm B, and whether any disclosure of health data is legally required or task-necessary under Norm A. Norm A itself contains disclosure exceptions; the provisions do not state that confidentiality must be achieved through the prohibited consent condition.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that, for the same service and trigger, the only legally possible way to comply with Norm A is to make access conditional on the user’s consent under Article 11.7(1), with no possibility of restricted disclosure, anonymisation, another lawful basis, or a statutory exception, could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Conversely, confirmation that no health data are processed would eliminate the overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A concerns confidentiality and permitted disclosure of health data; Norm B concerns conditioning service access on a specified form of user consent. Joint compliance is possible without using that consent condition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke persoonlijk gegevens verwerkt en op hem niet reeds uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift een geheimhoudingsplicht rust, is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens, behoudens voor zover de wet hem tot mededeling verplicht of uit zijn taak de noodzaak voortvloeit dat de gegevens worden meegedeeld aan anderen die krachtens het eerste, tweede of derde lid bevoegd zijn tot verwerking daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_actor: A data controller processing health data who is also an electronic communications network or service provider capable of processing subscriber or user location data, or an entity/person acting under that provider’s processing arrangements where the duties otherwise apply.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor processes protected personal/health data and, in the context of communication to a public emergency number, has relevant location data concerning a subscriber or user. The provisions overlap only if the same actor is subject to both regimes and the location data are also covered by the confidentiality duty.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the controller to keep the data confidential, unless the law requires disclosure or the controller’s task makes it necessary to disclose the data to others who are authorised under the referenced provisions to process them.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the provider, when communication over a public emergency number is handled, to simultaneously provide the relevant location data to the designated public-service emergency-number managers, even where the subscriber or user temporarily prevented processing of the relevant location data under Article 11.5a(5).
verdict.compliant_alternative: The duties can be jointly satisfied by treating the emergency disclosure as a disclosure required by law under Norm A’s express exception, and limiting the disclosure to the relevant location data and the legally designated emergency-number managers. The confidentiality duty continues to govern any use or disclosure beyond that required emergency transmission.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not establish whether the emergency-number managers are persons authorised to process the data under Norm A’s referenced first, second or third paragraphs, nor whether the particular location data qualify as health data covered by Norm A. It also does not specify the safeguards governing the emergency disclosure.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if the emergency disclosure were not legally required or otherwise covered by Norm A’s disclosure exception, and no other lawful disclosure route existed; or if Norm A expressly prohibited disclosure even where another law requires it. Conversely, proof that the data are outside Norm A’s scope would eliminate the overlap rather than create a conflict.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties. Norm A itself permits disclosure where the law requires it, while Norm B requires the specified emergency disclosure. The apparent tension is therefore reconciled by Norm A’s express exception.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the designated administrator under Norm B, if that administrator is also the data controller or another person subject to the confidentiality duty in Norm A.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both could apply when the administrator/data controller processes or provides the data covered by Norm B and the data are also health data processed under one of the situations referred to in Norm A, including where the supplied data do not correspond to the physical address of the network connection point.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the data controller, where not already bound by a professional, official, statutory, or contractual duty of confidentiality, to keep the data confidential, subject to disclosure required by law or necessary for the controller’s task to other persons authorised to process them under the relevant preceding paragraphs.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the designated administrator to reimburse the costs associated with providing the specified data, including the additional category of data where those data do not correspond to the physical address of the network connection point.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actor can maintain confidentiality while providing the data only to legally authorised recipients, using a legally required or task-necessary disclosure route, and reimburse the associated provision costs. The reimbursement duty does not itself require public disclosure of the data; if needed, disclosure could be restricted to authorised recipients or otherwise handled through a lawful confidential process.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish whether the administrator under Norm B is the same person as the data controller under Norm A, whether the data supplied under Norm B are health data, whether disclosure is legally required or task-necessary, or who the authorised recipients are. Norm B’s referenced first-lid data categories and triggering provisions are also not supplied.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if Norm B were interpreted to require disclosure of the relevant health data to a recipient who is not authorised under Norm A and no statutory disclosure obligation or task necessity applied, with no lawful restricted-disclosure or fallback procedure available. The identity of the administrator and the nature of the data would be decisive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not mutually exclusive: Norm A regulates confidentiality and permits specified lawful or necessary disclosures, while Norm B regulates reimbursement of costs for providing data. On the supplied text, both can be performed together.
