verdict.unresolved_exception: Onopgelost blijft welke concrete diensten, organisaties en certificeringsvoorschriften feitelijk overlappen, en of bij openbaarmaking bijzondere vertrouwelijkheids- of gegevensbeschermingsbeperkingen gelden. Ook is niet vastgesteld dat dezelfde actor beide rollen vervult.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: De uitkomst zou kunnen veranderen als blijkt dat dezelfde actor in dezelfde concrete situatie zowel de toegang volgens norm A moet toestaan als krachtens norm B informatie openbaar moet maken die norm A of een toepasselijke specifieke geheimhoudingsregel verbiedt, zonder mogelijkheid tot anonimisering, beperkte openbaarmaking of een andere wettelijke uitzondering.
verdict.criterion_fired: Geen contradictie: norm A is een discretionaire bevoegdheid over toegang tot bepaalde diensten, terwijl norm B een openbaarmakingsplicht voor toezichthoudende autoriteiten en een registertaak voor het Comité bevat. De normen schrijven geen onderling onverenigbare handelingen voor en een gezamenlijke naleving is plausibel.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 3 van dit artikel bedoelde voorschriften en de in artikel 42, lid 5, bedoelde criteria worden door de toezichthoudende autoriteit in een eenvoudig toegankelijke vorm openbaar gemaakt.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie or other actor involved in providing or accessing the designated electronic services under Norm A, but Norm B specifically binds members and staff of each toezichthoudende autoriteit. The texts do not establish that these are the same actors.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could be relevant in a digital-service or supervisory context, but no specific factual circumstance in the texts shows that the use of the public identification means under Norm A coincides with confidential information coming to the knowledge of supervisory-authority members or staff under Norm B.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A confers a competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organisations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B imposes professional secrecy on members and staff of every supervisory authority, during and after their term, regarding confidential information learned in performing their tasks or exercising their powers; during their term this particularly covers reports of infringements by natural persons.
verdict.compliant_alternative: No conflict-resolution measure is needed on the stated facts. If a supervisory authority or its staff were involved, the identification-based access could be provided or used while confidential information and infringement reports remained restricted to authorised persons and were not disclosed contrary to professional secrecy.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether any actor subject to Norm A is also a member or staff member of a supervisory authority, and whether use of the identification means would entail disclosure of confidential information covered by Norm B. The provisions also do not specify the relationship between the designated organisations and supervisory authorities.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that the same actor, for the same trigger, is required by Norm A to disclose or make publicly accessible information that Norm B requires that actor to keep secret—and that restricted disclosure, anonymisation, or another lawful process cannot satisfy both—could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Conversely, proof that the actors or circumstances are distinct would confirm no conflict.
verdict.criterion_fired: The texts do not establish a shared actor and shared triggering circumstance, nor do they show mutually exclusive duties. A firm NOT_A_CONFLICT conclusion is plausible, but the requested comparison lacks enough factual linkage to rule out an overlap without guessing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de vertrouwelijke informatie die hun bij de uitvoering van hun taken of de uitoefening van hun bevoegdheden ter kennis is gekomen, geldt voor het lid of de leden en de personeelsleden van elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zowel tijdens hun ambtstermijn als daarna het beroepsgeheim, zulks overeenkomstig Unierecht of lidstatelijk recht. Tijdens hun ambtstermijn geldt het beroepsgeheim met name voor meldingen van inbreuken op deze verordening door natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly identified actor is subject to both provisions. Norm A concerns the minister exercising delegated regulatory competence; Norm B concerns the lead supervisory authority under the GDPR.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern electronic services or personal-data-related regulatory contexts, but the provisions do not establish the same triggering facts or legal procedure.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and related facility may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organisations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the lead supervisory authority, when it rejects or considers irrelevant or unsubstantiated a relevant and reasoned objection submitted within four weeks, to refer the matter to the Article 63 consistency mechanism.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not establish that the minister and the lead supervisory authority are the same actor, that the same proceeding triggers both provisions, or that exercising Norm A's competence would affect the Article 60 procedure.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: Facts showing that the same actor, in the same proceeding and on the same trigger, must exercise Norm A's competence while being legally prohibited from or unable to make the Article 60 referral could change the assessment; the relevant surrounding provisions and institutional roles would also be needed.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not show a shared actor and shared circumstance sufficiently to test whether their duties are mutually exclusive. Similar subject matter alone does not establish contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien één van de andere betrokken toezichthoudende autoriteiten binnen een termijn van vier weken na te zijn geraadpleegd overeenkomstig lid 3 van dit artikel een relevant en gemotiveerd bezwaar tegen het ontwerpbesluit indient, onderwerpt de leidende toezichthoudende autoriteit, indien zij het relevante en gemotiveerde bezwaar afwijst of het niet relevant of niet gemotiveerd acht, de aangelegenheid aan het in artikel 63 bedoelde coherentiemechanisme.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a competent authority or designated organisation only insofar as it falls within the relevant statutory roles; the texts do not establish that the same actor is necessarily subject to both provisions.
verdict.shared_circumstance: There is no sufficiently established shared trigger. Norm A concerns a ministerial regulation permitting use of a public identification means for access to specified electronic services of designated organisations. Norm B concerns a Member State empowering competent authorities to impose measures following an infringement of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants a competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and the relevant facility may also be used to access specified electronic services, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires Member States to empower competent authorities to impose, among other measures, public communications identifying the infringing natural or legal person and describing the infringement.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Both could be satisfied by authorising the identification means for qualifying services while a competent authority separately uses the enforcement powers under Norm B only for an established infringement, with any disclosure limited to the information and circumstances permitted by applicable law.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions supplied do not identify the actors' institutional overlap, the specific services or infringement, or any confidentiality, data-protection, or national-law limits that might restrict a public announcement or the use of the identification means.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A specific rule or factual situation showing that the authorised use under Norm A necessarily requires conduct that Norm B requires the authority to stop, or that Norm B's mandatory public disclosure would necessarily violate a binding confidentiality or identification restriction applicable to the same actor and trigger, could change the assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A is a permissive competence concerning access to electronic services; Norm B is an enforcement-empowerment requirement concerning measures after an infringement. Their subject matter and triggers are not shown to be incompatible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het doen uitgaan van openbare mededelingen, met inbegrip van openbare verklaringen, waarbij de identiteit van de natuurlijke of rechtspersoon die de inbreuk heeft begaan, en de aard van de inbreuk worden bekendgemaakt.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under Norm A and a bevoegde autoriteit exchanging information under Norm B, but the provisions do not establish that these are the same actor or that an aangewezen organisatie is a bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern electronic or information-related activity involving an organisation or authority, but no specific factual scenario in the texts establishes that Norm A's access arrangement and Norm B's exchange of confidential information occur together.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence to determine by ministerial regulation that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organisations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires information exchanged between competent authorities under the Regulation, concerning operational or business conditions or other economic or personal matters, to be treated as confidential and subject to professional secrecy, unless the competent authority declares at the time of communication that disclosure is permitted or disclosure is necessary for judicial proceedings.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The access competence in Norm A can be exercised while Norm B's information remains confidential—for example, by limiting the electronic service to authorised users, restricting disclosure, and applying professional-secrecy safeguards. If disclosure is needed, Norm B itself permits it where the stated exception applies.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not resolve whether a designated organisation under Norm A is also a competent authority under Norm B, whether the electronic service would expose information covered by Article 55, or whether any disclosure would fall within Article 55's declaration or judicial-proceedings exceptions.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if the same actor and trigger were established and Norm A necessarily required public disclosure or unrestricted access to information that Article 55 absolutely forbids disclosing, with no applicable Article 55 exception or confidentiality-preserving implementation. Conversely, proof that the actors or subject matters are distinct would remove even the potential overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not establish a shared actor, shared trigger, or an unavoidable clash between the access competence in Norm A and the confidentiality obligation in Norm B. Joint compliance appears possible, but the factual relationship is insufficiently specified for a firm NOT_A_CONFLICT determination.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alle uitwisseling van informatie tussen de bevoegde autoriteiten krachtens deze verordening die betrekking heeft op exploitatie- of bedrijfsomstandigheden en andere economische of persoonlijke zaken, wordt als vertrouwelijk beschouwd en valt onder de vereisten van het beroepsgeheim, tenzij de bevoegde autoriteit op het moment van de mededeling verklaart dat deze informatie kan worden bekendgemaakt of de bekendmaking ervan noodzakelijk is voor gerechtelijke procedures.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under Norm A and a rechtshandhavingsinstantie under Norm B, but the texts do not establish that these are the same actor or that every designated organization is a law-enforcement authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Use or access involving electronic services or systems in the public domain/public spaces. Norm B specifically concerns real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law-enforcement purposes; Norm A concerns use of a public identification means and related facility to access designated electronic services, excluding specified categories of services.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence to establish, by ministerial regulation, that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access designated electronic services of designated organizations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires that the relevant law-enforcement authority complete a fundamental-rights impact assessment and register the system in the EU database before use, while allowing registration after commencement without undue delay in duly justified emergencies; use must also comply with necessary and proportionate safeguards and conditions.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular designated organization under Norm A is also a law-enforcement authority using a real-time remote biometric-identification system, and whether the public identification means or facility covered by Norm A is the AI system regulated by Norm B. Even if both apply, Norm A's permissive competence can coexist with Norm B's conditions and does not authorize use contrary to them.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A permits a ministerial regulation concerning access to designated electronic services, whereas Norm B conditions a specific law-enforcement use of real-time remote biometric identification on safeguards, impact assessment, and registration. Joint compliance is therefore plausible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het gebruik van het systeem voor biometrische identificatie op afstand in real time in openbare ruimten wordt alleen toegestaan indien de rechtshandhavingsinstantie een in artikel 27 voorziene effectbeoordeling op het gebied van de grondrechten heeft uitgevoerd en het systeem volgens artikel 49 in de EU-databank heeft geregistreerd. In naar behoren gemotiveerde spoedeisende gevallen kan echter met het gebruik van dergelijke systemen worden begonnen zonder de systemen in de EU-databank te registreren, op voorwaarde dat die registratie zonder onnodige vertraging wordt voltooid.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under Norm A that is also an aanmeldende autoriteit under Norm B, if the relevant statutory roles overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor uses or enables the public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility for access to designated electronic services, while also holding information obtained under Article 78 that must be handled confidentially.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants competence: by ministerial regulation, it may be determined that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organisations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained by them in accordance with Article 78 is treated confidentially.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Permit the specified access while restricting disclosure and processing of Article 78 information to authorised persons and purposes, with confidentiality safeguards, anonymisation or redaction where information is displayed, and no disclosure of protected information through the access service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether the particular electronic service would expose Article 78 information, nor the precise scope of the confidentiality requirement or any exceptions under Article 78. Norm A is a competence, not an unconditional duty to provide access.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if a binding ministerial regulation or the design of the service required disclosure of particular Article 78 information to users, and that disclosure were incompatible with the confidentiality duty with no lawful redaction, access restriction, or other fallback available.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A authorises possible access arrangements, while Norm B requires confidentiality; the access arrangement can be implemented with confidentiality safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under Norm A and an aanmeldende autoriteit under Norm B, but the texts do not establish that these categories overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could both be relevant when an organization uses a public identification means or related facility to access designated electronic services and, separately, has obtained information under Article 78. No common triggering circumstance is expressly stated.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants a competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organizations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained by them in accordance with Article 78 is treated confidentially.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Permit the authorized access under Norm A while restricting any Article 78 information handled under Norm B to confidential use and disclosure, with access controls, anonymisation or redaction where necessary. Nothing in Norm A requires disclosure of confidential Article 78 information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a designated organization is also a notifying authority, nor do they provide the content of Article 78 or any confidentiality exceptions. Those matters could affect application but do not establish a contradiction on the supplied text.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that Norm A necessarily requires the same notifying authority to disclose specific Article 78 information publicly or to an unauthorized recipient, and that such disclosure is forbidden by Article 45 without exception, could change the verdict. Evidence that the actor categories cannot overlap would instead eliminate even the potential shared application.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger: Norm A is a conditional competence concerning access to electronic services, while Norm B is a confidentiality obligation concerning information obtained under Article 78. Joint compliance remains possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under BWBR0048156 and a nationale bevoegde autoriteit under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, but the texts do not establish that the same entity necessarily has both statuses.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The rules could overlap when a designated organisation that is also a national competent authority uses a public identification means and the related facility to access specified electronic services, while carrying out its tasks under the AI Act.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A confers a competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organisations, subject to the stated exclusions.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges national competent authorities, when performing their tasks, to comply with the confidentiality obligations laid down in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The authority could use the authorised public identification means and facility for the specified access while restricting handling or disclosure of information as necessary to comply with Article 78 confidentiality obligations, including access controls or a confidential/fallback process if needed.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular designated organisation is also a national competent authority, whether the relevant ministerial regulation has actually been adopted, and what Article 78 specifically requires in the relevant situation. Norm A also excludes certain categories of services, but the text does not show that the service at issue falls within them.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction would require facts showing that the authorised access under Norm A necessarily entails an act or disclosure that Article 78 absolutely prohibits, with no possibility of restricted access, anonymisation, confidentiality safeguards, or another compliant process. Conversely, proof that the entities or circumstances do not overlap would eliminate even the potential interaction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties. Norm A is a conditional competence concerning permitted use of an identification means; Norm B is a confidentiality obligation. The text supports simultaneous compliance and contains no requirement that exercising Norm A's competence breach Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij de uitvoering van hun taken voldoen de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten aan de in artikel 78 vastgelegde vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially designated organizations under BWBR0048156 and the public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, but the provisions do not establish that these are the same actors.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Only at a high level could both relate to an organization or authority using a public identification means or facility to access specified electronic services while handling information or documentation obtained under Article 77. The texts do not establish that Article 77 information is involved in the Article 8 access context.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 8 grants a competence: by ministerial regulation it may be determined that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organizations, excluding services for exercising a public task, in the public interest, or involving processing of the citizen service number.
verdict.requirement_b: Information or documentation obtained under Article 77 by the authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) must be processed in accordance with the confidentiality obligations described in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The actors could use the public identification means or facility for an Article 8-authorized service while processing any Article 77 information under Article 78 confidentiality safeguards, such as restricting access and disclosure to authorized persons. Article 8 does not require disclosure of Article 77 information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not identify whether a designated organization under Article 8 is also an Article 77(1) authority or body, whether the relevant service involves Article 77 information, or what Article 78 specifically requires. Any detailed compatibility question therefore remains unresolved, although no textual conflict is shown.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that Article 8 necessarily requires disclosure or processing of Article 77 information in a manner prohibited by Article 78 could change the verdict. Conversely, confirmation that the actors or circumstances never overlap would make the absence of a shared application definitive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, non-mutually-exclusive rules: Article 8 is a conditional competence concerning permitted access to electronic services, while Article 77 imposes confidentiality-compliant processing of information obtained under that article. Neither provision requires what the other forbids.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a designated organization under Norm A that is also a national public authority or body covered by Norm B, or an authority interacting with such an organization; the texts do not establish that the same actor necessarily holds both competences.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern electronic services or AI-related activities involving a public identification means or related provision, but the provisions do not establish the same concrete triggering situation. Norm B applies when access to documentation concerning a high-risk AI system is needed to exercise a fundamental-rights enforcement mandate.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A authorizes a ministerial regulation to determine that a public identification means and the provision referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used to access specified electronic services of designated organizations, excluding services for a public task, in the public interest, or involving processing of the citizen service number.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes national public authorities or bodies responsible for monitoring or enforcing Union-law fundamental-rights obligations concerning listed high-risk AI systems to request and inspect documentation prepared or maintained under the Regulation, in an accessible language and format, when access is needed for effective exercise of their mandate within their jurisdiction; the authority must notify the market-surveillance authority of the Member State.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The competences can be exercised cumulatively: access under Norm A can be limited to the specified eligible electronic services, while a qualifying authority separately requests and inspects the necessary AI documentation under Norm B and gives the required notification. If disclosure or access raises a separate legal restriction, the authority could provide only the documentation necessary for its mandate in the required accessible format, subject to any applicable confidentiality or data-protection safeguards.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether a designated organization under Norm A is also the documentation holder or a qualifying authority under Norm B, nor whether any other confidentiality, data-protection, jurisdictional, or access restrictions apply. Norm A also excludes certain categories of electronic services, while Norm B does not address identification means or those exclusions.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if the same actor and identical trigger were established and another binding rule made the Norm B authority’s required documentation access impossible whenever the Norm A service-access arrangement applied, with no lawful restricted-disclosure or other fallback. Conversely, proof that the relevant service is excluded by Norm A or that no high-risk AI documentation is needed under Norm B would remove the apparent overlap rather than create a conflict.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions confer distinct, non-exclusive competences and do not require mutually incompatible conduct. The texts do not show that one competence requires what the other forbids, and a cumulative or appropriately limited exercise is possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan worden bepaald dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens kan worden gebruikt voor de toegang tot daarbij bepaalde elektronische diensten, anders dan diensten ter uitoefening van een publieke taak, in het algemeen belang of waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, van aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen die de nakoming van verplichtingen krachtens Unierecht ter bescherming van grondrechten, waaronder het recht op non-discriminatie, met betrekking tot het gebruik van de in bijlage III vermelde AI-systemen met een hoog risico controleren of handhaven, zijn bevoegd om krachtens deze verordening opgestelde of bijgehouden documentatie in een toegankelijke taal en een toegankelijk formaat aan te vragen en in te zien wanneer toegang tot die documentatie nodig is voor het doeltreffend uitoefenen van de bevoegdheden onder hun mandaat binnen de grenzen van hun rechtsgebied.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Only at a broad level: both provisions concern ministerial action involving electronic identification or electronic services. The text does not establish the same concrete triggering situation. Article 8 concerns authorising use of a public identification means for access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number; Article 11 concerns deciding an application for recognition where serious danger exists.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 8 gives Onze Minister a competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant minister, to determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 11 requires Onze Minister to refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including where there is a serious danger that the recognition will be used to commit criminal offences, exploit criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not state how Article 8's competence interacts with a possible Article 11 refusal, nor whether a particular use authorised under Article 8 could also constitute a serious danger under Article 11. That relationship is unresolved, but no mutually exclusive duties are shown.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Article 8 is a discretionary competence to authorise a specified use, while Article 11 is a mandatory refusal duty concerning an application for recognition when serious danger exists. Both could be complied with, for example by exercising Article 8 only where its conditions are met and refusing any Article 11 application meeting the serious-danger condition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the Minister)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions may concern the Minister in the context of regulated electronic data-access or identification services, but the texts do not establish that the same concrete service or proceeding necessarily triggers both rules.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 8, the Minister has competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible Minister, to determine that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a system for electronic data exchange processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 11, the Minister must recognise an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst if that service satisfies the rules established for it by or under a general administrative measure.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a service covered by Article 11 is also the same facility or access arrangement covered by Article 8, and whether any applicable general administrative-measure rules or ministerial regulation impose additional conditions. Nothing in the quoted text makes the competence in Article 8 incompatible with the recognition duty in Article 11.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Article 8 grants a conditional competence, while Article 11 imposes a conditional recognition duty; both could be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the Minister responsible under the relevant provisions)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions may concern the Minister in the context of regulating or authorizing digital identification means or related services, but the texts do not establish that the same concrete transaction or trigger necessarily activates both rules.
verdict.requirement_a: The Minister may, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the other Minister concerned, determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organizations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: The Minister must recognize an issuer of means for a business or organizational means and its associated assurance level if the service and means comply with rules laid down by or pursuant to an order in council.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular identification means or issuer could simultaneously fall within both provisions and whether additional rules under an order in council or ministerial regulation impose constraints. Nothing in the quoted texts makes the competence in Article 8 incompatible with the recognition duty in Article 11.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions address different legal acts and objects: Article 8 grants a conditional competence to authorize use of a public identification means for specified access, while Article 11 imposes a conditional recognition duty concerning an issuer, a business/organizational means, and its assurance level. They do not require mutually exclusive conduct, and both could be complied with where their respective conditions are met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een middelenuitgever met betrekking tot een door die dienst uit te geven bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel en het bijbehorende betrouwbaarheidsniveau, indien de dienst en het middel voldoen aan de daartoe bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister, bestuursorganen, and aangewezen organisaties could potentially be subject to both rules, insofar as the relevant organization and ministerial authority are involved.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Use of a public identification means and the provision referred to in Article 5(1)(b) to provide access to an electronic data-exchange system in which the citizen service number is processed, with the minister acting in agreement with the relevant minister; the second rule applies when processing personal data is necessary for statutory tasks and obligations.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants Onze Minister a competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant minister, to determine that the public identification means and provision may also be used for designated organizations to grant access to a non-electronic-service electronic data-exchange system processing the citizen service number.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges Onze Minister, administrative bodies, and designated organizations to process personal data, including the citizen service number, insofar as necessary for properly performing their statutory tasks and obligations, especially secure access to electronic services and preventing misuse.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify all conditions governing the legality or necessity of processing in the Article 8 access scenario, nor whether a particular processing operation is necessary for the statutory tasks. Nothing in the text makes the competence in Norm A require processing that Norm B forbids; Norm B instead permits or requires necessary processing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different, compatible legal effects: Norm A confers a conditional competence to authorize a form of access, while Norm B requires necessary personal-data processing. Neither rule requires what the other forbids, and joint compliance is plausible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister, alsmede bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties verwerken persoonsgegevens, waaronder het burgerservicenummer, voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor de goede uitvoering van hun taken en verplichtingen ingevolge deze wet, in het bijzonder het bieden van goede en veilige toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening en het voorkomen van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_actor: The Minister under Norm A; officials designated by the Minister under Norm B (not necessarily the same individual, and Norm B concerns supervision by designated officials).
verdict.shared_circumstance: Norm A concerns authorizing use of a public identification means and related facility for access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, outside electronic-service systems, with agreement of the relevant Minister. Norm B concerns supervision of compliance with Article 8(1) by designated officials when provincial-level administrative bodies are involved.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants the Minister competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant Minister, to determine that the specified identification means and facility may also be used by designated organizations for access to the described system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B assigns designated officials responsibility for supervising compliance with provisions including Article 8(1) by provincial-level administrative bodies.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify the precise scope of the supervision or how it operates in relation to a particular exercise of the Minister's competence, but nothing indicates that supervision forbids or displaces that competence.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose complementary competences: one permits a Minister to make a determination, while the other assigns officials to supervise compliance with Article 8(1). They do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger, and joint compliance is possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Met het toezicht op de naleving van het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 3, 6, 7, 8, eerste lid en 15 door bestuursorganen op het niveau van de provincies zijn belast de bij besluit van Onze Minister aangewezen ambtenaren.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the Minister)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's exercise of statutory authority in the context of systems involving electronic data exchange or conduct regulated by the Act. However, Article 17's competence is triggered specifically by an infringement of the provisions listed there, while Article 8 concerns designation and permitted use of a public identification means.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 8 gives the Minister, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible Minister, the competence to determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a system for electronic data exchange in which the citizen service number is processed, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 17 gives the Minister the competence to impose an administrative fine, up to the fifth-category statutory amount, on specified persons responsible for violations of the provisions listed in Article 17, per violation.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not establish whether a particular use authorised under Article 8 could also constitute a violation of one of the provisions listed in Article 17. Even if it could, the provisions provide different, potentially cumulative powers rather than mutually exclusive duties; the precise interaction depends on the content of the referenced provisions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not require incompatible conduct. Article 8 authorises a regulatory determination concerning use of an identification means, whereas Article 17 authorises sanctions for specified violations. Both competences can be exercised consistently, and Article 17 does not prohibit an Article 8 determination.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan degene die handelt in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 9, vierde, zevende of achtste lid, 11, 13 en 14, tweede en derde lid, daartoe opdracht heeft gegeven of feitelijk leiding geeft aan de rechtspersoon die in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 13, eerste, tweede, derde of vierde lid, een bestuurlijke boete opleggen van ten hoogste het bedrag dat is vastgesteld voor de vijfde categorie, bedoeld in artikel 23, vierde lid, van het Wetboek van Strafrecht, per overtreding die is begaan.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister and the officials designated by ministerial decision, but not necessarily in the same capacity
verdict.shared_circumstance: The use or implementation of the public identification means and the facility under Article 5(1)(b) for access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-services system; Article 17 concerns supervision of compliance with Article 8(2) and (3), while Article 8 as quoted does not specify a paragraph.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister a competence: by ministerial regulation, and in agreement with the responsible Minister, the Minister may determine that the public identification means and facility may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to the specified data-exchange system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B assigns designated officials the competence/duty to supervise compliance with Article 8(2) and (3), as well as Article 4.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text of Article 8 does not identify its paragraph number, whereas Article 17 expressly refers only to Article 8, second and third paragraphs. It is therefore unresolved whether the quoted Article 8 provision is within the scope of the supervision rule. Even if it is, supervision and ministerial authorization are compatible functions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor. Norm A authorizes a ministerial determination subject to inter-ministerial agreement; Norm B concerns supervision by designated officials. Both can operate simultaneously, and the text contains no prohibition or incompatible requirement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Met het toezicht op de naleving van het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 4 en het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 8, tweede en derde lid, zijn belast de bij besluit van Onze Minister aangewezen ambtenaren.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Use of an identification means to provide or obtain access to an electronic system/service; however, the provisions concern different types of systems and different circumstances.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A authorizes the Minister, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible Minister, to determine that a public identification means and the provision referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organizations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes the Minister to interrupt, or cause the interruption of, access to electronic services through a specified permitted identification means or recognized business/organizational means when misuse or improper use of that means is suspected.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify how an interruption under Article 18 would affect any access arrangement established under Article 8, nor does it define the relationship between the means or systems covered. Any actual overlap would depend on whether the same identification means is used and whether the Article 18 suspicion exists.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both provisions confer discretionary competences on the Minister, but they do not impose mutually exclusive duties. Article 8 concerns authorizing use for access to a non-electronic-services data-exchange system, while Article 18 concerns interrupting access to electronic services upon suspected misuse. The texts permit both competences to be exercised, and no direct prohibition or mandatory incompatibility is stated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening via een welbepaald toegelaten identificatiemiddel of erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel onderbreken of doen onderbreken bij het vermoeden van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van het desbetreffende middel.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister, in relation to designated organizations and other relevant administrative bodies or organs
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions may both be relevant where the public identification means and related facility are used for access to a data-exchange system involving the citizen service number, and costs arise in connection with implementation of the statutory scheme. However, Article 21 expressly concerns costs associated with Articles 5 and 9, not Article 8 itself.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 8 gives Onze Minister a competence, exercisable by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible minister, to determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used for designated organizations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 21 requires Onze Minister to charge the costs incurred by the State in connection with implementation of Articles 5 and 9 to the relevant administrative bodies, designated organizations, and other organs, with further rules set by ministerial regulation.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is not clear from the supplied text whether any costs connected specifically with an Article 8 determination or use fall within the cost-allocation rule, because Article 21 refers expressly to Articles 5 and 9. That scope issue does not create mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, compatible functions: Article 8 confers a conditional regulatory competence, while Article 21 imposes a cost-charging obligation. Neither requires conduct that the other forbids, and Article 21's stated scope does not establish a contradiction with Article 8.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kosten die het Rijk maakt samenhangend met de uitvoering van de artikelen 5 en 9 worden door Onze Minister ten laste gebracht van de bestuursorganen, aangewezen organisaties en andere organen die het betreft. Bij ministeriële regeling worden hierover regels gesteld.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the public authority or organization disclosing numbers/data and, separately, the minister deciding on use of a public identification means; the texts do not establish that these are the same actor
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both concern handling or access involving electronic systems or data, but Norm B applies specifically to disclosure of numbers and data for combating misuse of a public-services emergency number, while Norm A concerns ministerial authorization of use of a public identification means for access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants a competence: the Minister may, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible Minister, determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organizations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires that disclosure of numbers and data for combating misuse of a public-services emergency number be made only to a person charged under Articles 141 or 142 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with investigating criminal offences.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular disclosure or access operation would simultaneously fall within Norm B's specific purpose and recipient restriction and Norm A's authorization framework. The provisions do not state that either rule overrides or defers to the other, but they also do not require mutually exclusive conduct.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose incompatible duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A confers a conditional ministerial competence to authorize use; Norm B restricts a specific disclosure to specified investigative recipients. Authorization of access under Norm A can coexist with compliance with Norm B's recipient limitation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Verstrekking van nummers en gegevens met het oog op de bestrijding van het misbruik van een alarmnummer voor publieke diensten vindt slechts plaats aan degene die op grond van artikel 141 of 142 van het Wetboek van Strafvordering is belast met de opsporing van strafbare feiten.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the competent minister under Norm A and a supervisory authority under Norm B, but the texts do not establish that they are the same actor or that the minister is a supervisory authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern regulated electronic data or identification arrangements involving personal data, but Norm B is triggered by specified requirements and criteria under GDPR Articles 42(5) and 43(3), whereas Norm A concerns authorising use of a public identification means for access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the minister a competence, exercisable by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the minister concerned, to determine that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used for designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges the supervisory authority to publish, in an easily accessible form, the requirements referred to in Article 43(3) and the criteria referred to in Article 42(5), and to communicate those requirements and criteria to the Committee; the Committee must collect and publish the certification mechanisms and data-protection seals in a register.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The minister can exercise the Norm A competence only through the required ministerial regulation and interministerial agreement, while the supervisory authority separately publishes and communicates the certification requirements and criteria as required by Norm B. If the same institution were involved, it could keep the authorisation decision and the required certification information distinct and publish the latter in an easily accessible form.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not state whether the minister and supervisory authority are institutionally the same actor, whether the authorised system is subject to a certification mechanism covered by Norm B, or whether any other GDPR requirements limit the proposed use. Norm B also does not expressly regulate or prohibit the authorisation described in Norm A.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that Norm A expressly required withholding or concealing the exact requirements and criteria that Norm B requires the supervisory authority to publish, or that the same actor was legally unable to perform both duties simultaneously, could change the verdict. Conversely, confirmation that the minister is not the supervisory authority or that the system is outside the certification context would further establish no overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A confers an authorisation competence; Norm B requires publication and communication of certification requirements and criteria. The texts contain no prohibition in Norm B on granting access and no duty in Norm A to suppress the information required to be published.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 3 van dit artikel bedoelde voorschriften en de in artikel 42, lid 5, bedoelde criteria worden door de toezichthoudende autoriteit in een eenvoudig toegankelijke vorm openbaar gemaakt. De toezichthoudende autoriteiten delen die eisen en criteria ook mee aan het Comité. Het Comité verzamelt alle certificeringsmechanismen en gegevensbeschermingszegels in een register en maakt deze via geëigende kanalen openbaar.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly identified actor is subject to both norms. Norm A concerns Onze Minister exercising a competence; Norm B concerns members and staff of a supervisory authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern public-sector digital data contexts, but the text does not establish the same actor, transaction, or triggering situation. Norm A applies when determining use of a public identification means for access to a data-exchange system processing a citizen service number; Norm B applies when supervisory-authority personnel learn confidential information in performing their tasks or exercising powers.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister a competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant Minister, to determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-service system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges members and staff of every supervisory authority to maintain professional secrecy regarding confidential information learned in performing their tasks or exercising their powers, both during and after their term; during their term this specifically includes reports of infringements by natural persons.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister may exercise the competence under Norm A while supervisory-authority members and staff continue to restrict disclosure of confidential information under Norm B—for example, by granting access through the authorised identification mechanism without disclosing confidential supervisory information, and by using anonymised or otherwise lawfully limited information where reporting or data exchange is necessary.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how confidential supervisory information or infringement reports must be handled if the authorised data-exchange system is used, nor whether another applicable Union or national rule imposes disclosure or access duties. Norm B itself refers to applicable Union or Member State law, so any such additional rule remains unresolved.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if the same supervisory-authority personnel were required, as a condition of exercising Norm A, to disclose specific confidential information or natural-person infringement reports that Norm B absolutely forbids them to disclose, with no lawful restriction, anonymisation, or other compliant process available.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction: the provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A is a ministerial competence concerning authorised access; Norm B is a confidentiality obligation on supervisory-authority personnel. The text supports simultaneous compliance.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de vertrouwelijke informatie die hun bij de uitvoering van hun taken of de uitoefening van hun bevoegdheden ter kennis is gekomen, geldt voor het lid of de leden en de personeelsleden van elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zowel tijdens hun ambtstermijn als daarna het beroepsgeheim, zulks overeenkomstig Unierecht of lidstatelijk recht. Tijdens hun ambtstermijn geldt het beroepsgeheim met name voor meldingen van inbreuken op deze verordening door natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly established shared actor: Norm A concerns the Minister (acting with the responsible Minister), while Norm B concerns the lead supervisory authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern institutional decisions involving electronic data systems or personal-data processing, but the provisions do not establish the same trigger or factual proceeding.
verdict.requirement_a: The Minister may, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the responsible Minister, determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a system for electronic data exchange in which the citizen service number is processed, other than a system for electronic service provision.
verdict.requirement_b: If another concerned supervisory authority submits a relevant and reasoned objection within four weeks after consultation, and the lead supervisory authority rejects the objection or considers it irrelevant or unreasoned, the lead supervisory authority must submit the matter to the consistency mechanism referred to in Article 63.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister can exercise Norm A only through the stated ministerial-regulation procedure and ministerial agreement, while the lead supervisory authority separately follows Norm B if its specific objection and rejection conditions arise. Nothing in either text requires the Minister to prevent or override referral to the consistency mechanism.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a particular ministerial decision under Norm A could itself constitute a GDPR draft decision or otherwise place the same institution in the role of lead supervisory authority. Even then, the texts contain no express mutually exclusive command; the applicable procedural roles and any other GDPR provisions would need examination.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that the same actor, in the same proceeding and trigger, is legally required by Norm A to adopt or maintain a decision that Norm B requires that actor to submit to the consistency mechanism—and that no procedural separation, modification, or other lawful alternative is available—could change the verdict. The identity of the actor and the existence of a GDPR objection under Article 60 are currently not established.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a competent Dutch minister under Norm A and a competent authority of a Member State under Norm B; the texts do not establish that these are the same legal actor.

verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the minister competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the minister concerned, to determine that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than an electronic-service system.

verdict.compliant_alternative: The minister may exercise Norm A only under its stated agreement and scope conditions, while the competent authority may impose Norm B's public communication separately, with any legally required safeguards or limits on disclosure. Nothing in the quoted provisions requires the Norm A access arrangement to disclose the identity or nature of an infringement, nor does Norm B prohibit establishing such an access arrangement.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not identify the actors, the alleged infringement, or any applicable confidentiality, data-protection, or national-law limits that might restrict the public communication. Norm B itself qualifies some measures by national law, but that qualification does not create a textual conflict with Norm A.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A conflict could become plausible if the same actor and trigger were established and another applicable rule or binding decision required the actor to maintain the Norm A access arrangement while simultaneously requiring it to cease that exact arrangement, or if public disclosure under Norm B necessarily and unlawfully prohibited the access use authorised under Norm A. Those facts are not present in the quoted text.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A confers a conditional competence; Norm B concerns the authority to impose sanctions or corrective measures after an infringement. Joint compliance remains possible.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a minister under Norm A and competent authorities under Norm B, but the provisions do not establish that the same actor is subject to both duties.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Exchange or access involving electronic data systems or information concerning economic, personal, or business matters. The texts do not establish that the same transaction or information exchange necessarily falls under both provisions.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant Minister, to determine that a public identification means and the facility referred to in Article 5(1)(b) may also be used by designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the citizen service number, other than a system for electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires information exchanged between competent authorities under the Regulation, concerning operational or business circumstances or other economic or personal matters, to be treated as confidential and subject to professional secrecy, unless the competent authority declares at the time of communication that it may be disclosed or disclosure is necessary for judicial proceedings.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister may authorize the described access while the competent authorities restrict any exchanged information to authorized recipients and maintain confidentiality and professional secrecy. If disclosure is needed, it may occur only under Norm B's stated exception—an express declaration at the time of communication or necessity for judicial proceedings—without making the citizen-service-number system generally public.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular use authorized under Norm A would involve an exchange of information 'between the competent authorities krachtens deze verordening' within Norm B, and whether any disclosure would be covered by Norm B's exceptions. Norm A itself does not require disclosure.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that Norm A requires the same actor to disclose the covered information to persons not permitted to receive it under Norm B, with no applicable declaration or judicial-proceedings exception, could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Conversely, confirmation that the actors, information, or exchange fall outside Norm B would remove even the apparent overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger: Norm A confers a conditional competence to authorize access, while Norm B imposes confidentiality subject to express exceptions. Confidential access or a permitted disclosure can satisfy both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an aangewezen organisatie under Norm A and an aanmeldende autoriteit under Norm B, but the provisions do not establish that these categories overlap.

verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, by ministerial regulation and in agreement with the relevant Minister, to determine that a public identification means and the Article 5(1)(b) facility may also be used for designated organisations to grant access to a data-exchange system processing the burgerservicenummer, other than a system for electronic public services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained by them in accordance with Article 78 is treated confidentially.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The access competence in Norm A can be exercised while the relevant authority treats any information obtained under Article 78 confidentially—for example, by limiting access and disclosure to authorised purposes and applying confidentiality safeguards. Nothing in the quoted text requires public disclosure of the information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether an organisation authorised under Norm A is also an aanmeldende autoriteit, nor what information is obtained under Article 78 or the precise scope of the confidentiality requirement. verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that exercising Norm A necessarily requires disclosing information obtained under Article 78 in a manner prohibited by Norm B, or that the same actor is legally required both to disclose and to keep that information confidential, could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION.
verdict.criterion_fired: The quoted provisions impose no mutually exclusive duties: Norm A is a conditional ministerial competence concerning authorised access, whereas Norm B is a confidentiality obligation. They can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling kan Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het aangaat bepalen dat een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, tevens ten behoeve van aangewezen organisaties kan worden gebruikt voor het verlenen van toegang tot een systeem voor de elektronische uitwisseling van gegevens waarbij het burgerservicenummer wordt verwerkt, anders dan een systeem voor elektronische dienstverlening.
