verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister acting under the statutory framework for reliable and secure access to electronic services, but they do not establish the same specific trigger: Article 9 concerns non-compliance or serious reasons affecting an accreditation, while Article 19 concerns information about an infringement where disclosure is necessary for statutory tasks or services.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 9 gives the Minister competence to modify, suspend, or withdraw an accreditation; upon suspension or withdrawal, the holder may be required to continue activities for a specified period when necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 19 obliges the Minister to provide data and information to specified authorities, organizations, accredited holders, or recognized issuers/providers about an infringement of secure and reliable access, insofar as necessary for proper performance of their statutory tasks or services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether information disclosure under Article 19 is subject to confidentiality, data-protection, or other restrictions that could affect a particular disclosure. Nothing in the quoted text makes exercising the Article 9 competence incompatible with providing the required information under Article 19.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose different, potentially cumulative functions—Article 9 confers a regulatory competence concerning accreditation, while Article 19 imposes an information-disclosure obligation. Neither requires conduct that the other forbids, and joint compliance is possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning wijzigen, schorsen of intrekken indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid, de eisen, voorschriften of beperkingen bedoeld in het vierde lid, of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in het zesde lid. Bij schorsing en intrekking kan de houder worden verplicht zijn activiteiten voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.

verdict.shared_actor: De bevoegde regelgever/overheid (voor zover art. 22 de regels bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur laat stellen en art. 9 de bevoegdheid aan Onze Minister geeft)
verdict.shared_circumstance: De uitoefening van wettelijke bevoegdheden rond erkenning van identificatiemiddelen en toezicht/heffingen binnen hetzelfde wettelijke stelsel. De bepalingen hebben echter geen duidelijk identieke concrete trigger.
verdict.requirement_a: Art. 9 verleent Onze Minister de bevoegdheid een erkenning te wijzigen, schorsen of intrekken wanneer niet aan bepaalde eisen wordt voldaan of bij zwaarwegende redenen; bij schorsing of intrekking kan de houder bovendien worden verplicht activiteiten voort te zetten om betrouwbare toegang te continueren.

verdict.unresolved_exception: Het is niet duidelijk uit de aangeleverde teksten welke concrete actor precies de regels op grond van art. 22 moet stellen of hoe die heffingsregels zich verhouden tot de erkenningsbevoegdheid van art. 9. verdict.shared_circumstance: The administration of recognition applications under Articles 9 or 11, and supervision of compliance with requirements under Articles 9 or 13; Article 9 also concerns non-compliance with recognition requirements or serious reasons affecting reliable electronic access.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence to modify, suspend, or withdraw a recognition, and, upon suspension or withdrawal, to require the holder to continue activities for a specified period where necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives Onze Minister the competence to impose a cost-recovery levy, according to a tariff set by the Minister, for processing recognition applications and supervising compliance with Articles 9 and 13.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether any procedural, tariff, or statutory limits restrict exercising both competences in the same case. That uncertainty does not make the competences mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both norms confer compatible discretionary competences on the same actor. Norm A concerns recognition measures and possible continuity obligations; Norm B concerns cost-recovery levies for applications or supervision. Neither requires or prohibits conduct that the other forbids, and the text contains no mutually exclusive condition.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the competent minister), potentially in relation to providers subject to the continuity-plan provision
verdict.shared_circumstance: A continuity-related situation involving reliable access to electronic services and, under Norm B, failure of the relevant providers to agree on a joint continuity plan. The texts do not expressly establish that these are the same factual trigger.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence to modify, suspend, or withdraw an recognition when specified requirements are not met or for compelling reasons. Upon suspension or withdrawal, the holder may be required to continue activities for a period determined by the Minister insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives the Minister competence to issue instructions concerning the establishment of a joint continuity plan when the providers referred to in paragraph 4 cannot reach agreement on that plan.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister could exercise both competences in a coordinated manner: issue instructions to establish the joint continuity plan while, if necessary, suspending or withdrawing recognition and requiring the holder to continue activities temporarily to preserve reliable access. Nothing in either text requires the Minister to choose one measure to the exclusion of the other.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not identify the providers in Norm B, the recognition holder in Norm A, or the precise relationship between the two statutory regimes. It is therefore unresolved whether the same actor is subject to both provisions and whether any separate procedural or sector-specific limits apply.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A provision expressly stating that issuing continuity-plan instructions precludes suspension or withdrawal, or that suspension/withdrawal legally forbids the holder from continuing activities or participating in the plan, would change the assessment. The verdict could also change if the relevant actors or triggering circumstances were legally disjoint.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction: both provisions confer ministerial competences concerning continuity, but neither imposes a mutually exclusive duty or prohibits the exercise required by the other; the texts permit coordinated or sequential measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij schorsing en intrekking kan de houder worden verplicht zijn activiteiten voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de in het vierde lid bedoelde aanbieders geen overeenstemming kunnen bereiken over het gezamenlijke continuïteitsplan, kan Onze Minister voorschriften geven inzake het tot stand brengen van het plan.

verdict.shared_actor: Een aanmeldende autoriteit kan mogelijk ook Onze Minister zijn, voor zover die autoriteit een aanwijzing of erkenning beperkt, schorst of intrekt.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een aanwijzing/erkenning, waarbij de wijziging gevolgen kan hebben voor betrouwbare elektronische dienstverlening of certificaten.

verdict.unresolved_exception: De teksten stellen niet vast dat Onze Minister en de aanmeldende autoriteit dezelfde juridische actor zijn, noch dat een erkenning onder Norm A precies dezelfde aanwijzing betreft als onder Norm B. Ook is niet uitgewerkt hoe de continuïteitsverplichting uit Norm A zich praktisch verhoudt tot de certificaatmaatregelen uit Norm B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Geen tegenstrijdigheid: Norm A geeft een bevoegdheid en kan een continuïteitsmaatregel opleggen, terwijl Norm B een afzonderlijke rapportageplicht oplegt. De regels schrijven geen onderling onverenigbare handelingen voor en kunnen gelijktijdig worden nageleefd.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister / aangewezen ambtenaren or organizations within the relevant public administration; the texts do not establish that exactly the same actor must perform both functions

verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.

verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions may concern the same electronic-services regulatory framework, but the text does not establish that Article 9's recognition decision and Article 17's supervision of compliance with Articles 3, 6, 7, 8(1), and 15 arise for the same actor and trigger.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 9 requires the Minister to refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including serious danger to cybersecurity, state security, criminal misuse, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.

verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different types of legal consequences—an obligation to refuse recognition in specified circumstances and an allocation of supervisory competence. No mutually exclusive duties or prohibition of the supervisory function is shown; both can operate simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister’s exercise of authority under the same statutory framework, but they do not establish the same factual trigger: Article 9 concerns deciding an application for recognition where serious reasons oppose recognition, while Article 17 concerns an established violation of specified provisions, including Article 9.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 9 obliges the Minister to refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when serious reasons oppose recognition, including serious danger to cybersecurity, state security, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 17 authorizes, but does not oblige, the Minister to impose an administrative fine on specified persons for each violation of the listed provisions, including Article 9.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not specify how a particular Article 9 violation and a later or concurrent refusal decision interact, nor whether any procedural or proportionality limits apply to imposing a fine alongside refusal. Those issues do not make the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different and compatible legal effects: Article 9 requires refusal in specified circumstances, whereas Article 17 grants discretionary competence to impose a fine for violations. The fine power does not require granting recognition and therefore does not contradict refusal.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister and/or officials designated by Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: The administration and enforcement of the recognition requirements under this statutory scheme, potentially including applications or compliance concerning the provisions referenced in Articles 4 and 8(2)-(3).

verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister’s administration of the statutory system for electronic services, potentially involving an entity seeking or holding an erkenning and circumstances relevant to the safe and reliable access to electronic services. verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the Minister to refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including serious danger to cybersecurity or state security, criminal misuse, or danger to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.

The text permits both duties to be performed together and contains no mutually exclusive commands.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the Minister); potentially the relevant bestuursorganen, aangewezen organisaties and other organs for the cost-bearing consequence
verdict.shared_circumstance: The circumstances concern the execution of Article 9, including an application for recognition and, under Article 9, serious risks to cybersecurity, state security, criminal misuse, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 9, the Minister must refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including the specified serious dangers.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 21, the Minister charges the costs incurred by the State in connection with implementing Articles 5 and 9 to the relevant administrative bodies, designated organisations and other organs, subject to rules set by ministerial regulation.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provision does not specify how costs are allocated in a particular case or whether any ministerial-regulation exception applies. That uncertainty does not make the refusal duty and cost-allocation duty mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different actions and can be performed together: the Minister can refuse a recognition under Article 9 and also charge implementation costs under Article 21. Article 21 does not require granting recognition or otherwise prohibit refusal.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kosten die het Rijk maakt samenhangend met de uitvoering van de artikelen 5 en 9 worden door Onze Minister ten laste gebracht van de bestuursorganen, aangewezen organisaties en andere organen die het betreft.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister / the competent public authority responsible for recognition decisions and the charging framework
verdict.shared_circumstance: An application for recognition and related administrative handling under BWBR0048156; however, the quoted text of Article 22 does not expressly establish that its rule applies to the same decision or circumstances as Article 9.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 9 requires the Minister to refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when serious reasons oppose recognition, including serious danger to cybersecurity, state security, criminal misuse, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 22 requires rules to be established by or pursuant to a general administrative measure concerning the amount and imposition of a levy, with possible distinctions between categories of acts referred to in paragraph 1.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The quoted Article 22 text does not specify the levy’s precise application, timing, or interaction with an Article 9 refusal. Any issue concerning whether a levy may be imposed when recognition is refused is therefore unresolved, but no incompatible duties are stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different duties: Article 9 concerns refusing recognition in specified risk or non-compliance situations, while Article 22 concerns establishing rules for levies. Neither requires an act that the other forbids, and both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur worden regels gesteld over de hoogte en het opleggen van de heffing, waarbij onderscheid kan worden gemaakt tussen verschillende categorieën handelingen als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister acting in relation to electronic communications or electronic-service security, but Norm B has no express triggering condition and applies specifically to providers of public electronic communications networks or services.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the Minister to refuse recognition when the statutory requirements are not met or when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including serious danger to cybersecurity, state security, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes the Minister to impose on a provider of public electronic communications networks or services an obligation to take security-related measures within a specified period, including measures to prevent or resolve a security incident.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a particular recognition applicant is also a provider covered by Norm B and whether the concrete security measures imposed under Norm B could affect the recognition decision. The texts contain no mutually exclusive instruction and do not specify how the provisions interact in an individual case.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not require mutually exclusive conduct. Refusing recognition under Norm A and imposing security measures under Norm B can both occur, while Norm B's competence does not require granting recognition or otherwise prohibit refusal.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan een aanbieder van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten de verplichting opleggen om binnen een bepaalde termijn maatregelen te treffen

verdict.shared_actor: Een overheidsautoriteit die zowel als Onze Minister onder norm A en als aanmeldende autoriteit onder norm B optreedt; de teksten bewijzen niet dat dit steeds dezelfde autoriteit is.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Er zijn ernstige betrouwbaarheids-, veiligheids- of nalevingsproblemen rond een erkenning of aangemelde instantie, maar de normen stellen niet exact dezelfde feitelijke trigger vast.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A verplicht Onze Minister een erkenning te weigeren wanneer zwaarwegende redenen zich daartegen verzetten, waaronder ernstig gevaar voor cyberveiligheid, staatsveiligheid, strafbare feiten of de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B verplicht de aanmeldende autoriteit een kwestie onverwijld en zorgvuldig te onderzoeken wanneer zij voldoende reden heeft om te menen dat een aangemelde instantie niet meer aan artikel 31 voldoet of haar verplichtingen niet nakomt; na die conclusie moet zij de aanwijzing, indien passend, beperken, schorsen of intrekken, afhankelijk van de ernst.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Onopgelost blijft of een concrete instantie, erkenning en aanwijzing onder beide regelingen vallen en of de bevoegde autoriteiten dezelfde zijn. Ook bepaalt norm B dat de maatregel passend moet zijn en afhankelijk is van de ernst; zij schrijft niet in alle gevallen intrekking voor. De bepalingen bevatten geen expliciete voorrang- of verwijzingsregel.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichtingen zijn niet wederzijds exclusief: weigering van een erkenning onder norm A kan samengaan met onderzoek en, indien passend, beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een aanwijzing onder norm B. De teksten tonen geen situatie waarin de ene norm verplicht iets te doen wat de andere verbiedt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een erkenning indien niet wordt voldaan aan de eisen bedoeld in het tweede of derde lid. Hij weigert tevens indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een aanmeldende autoriteit voldoende reden heeft om van mening te zijn dat een aangemelde instantie niet meer aan de eisen van artikel 31 voldoet of haar verplichtingen niet nakomt, moet de aanmeldende autoriteit de kwestie onverwijld zo zorgvuldig mogelijk onderzoeken.

verdict.shared_actor: The minister or competent ministerial authority responsible for issuing regulations and recognizing services
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the regulatory and administrative treatment of identification-related services or facilities under BWBR0048156, but they do not establish the same concrete trigger or require the same act in the same circumstances.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 10, rules must be established by ministerial regulation concerning the use of public identification means and the facilities referred to in Article 5(1).
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 11, the Minister recognizes an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst if that service complies with rules laid down by or pursuant to an algemene maatregel van bestuur concerning that service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how ministerial regulations under Article 10 relate to the general administrative order rules governing recognition under Article 11, or whether any particular service or facility falls within both regimes. That relationship is unresolved, but no incompatible duties are stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, compatible functions: Article 10 authorizes or requires rulemaking about use, while Article 11 requires recognition of a qualifying service. Neither requires an act that the other forbids, and the text contains no mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling worden regels gesteld met betrekking tot het gebruik van publieke identificatiemiddelen en de voorzieningen, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: The minister responsible for issuing ministerial regulations
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the making of ministerial regulations, but they address different subject matters: public identification means and related facilities under Article 5(1) versus telephone-number identification in electronic communications.
verdict.requirement_a: The ministerial regulation must set rules concerning the use of public identification means and the facilities referred to in Article 5(1).
verdict.requirement_b: The ministerial regulation must set further rules concerning blocking and refusal, prevention of caller-number or individual-user identification, implementation of number identification in international electronic communications, and information by providers, users and subscribers about number identification.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how the ministerial rules should be coordinated if their subject matters overlap, nor whether one regulation or separate regulations must be used. Nothing in the text shows that compliance with one would prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose compatible rule-making competences concerning distinct, potentially overlapping aspects of identification; neither requires conduct that the other forbids, and both can be satisfied through coordinated or separate ministerial rules.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling worden regels gesteld met betrekking tot het gebruik van publieke identificatiemiddelen en de voorzieningen, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b:
Bij ministeriële regeling worden nadere regels gesteld met betrekking tot:

a.
mogelijkheden tot blokkering en weigering;

b.
de voorwaarden waaronder de abonnee de identificatie van het nummer van oproepende netwerkaansluitpunten dan wel een nummer waarmee een individuele gebruiker kan worden geïdentificeerd kan doen verhinderen;

c.
de wijze waarop uitvoering aan nummeridentificatie in het internationale elektronische communicatieverkeer kan worden gegeven, en

d.
de wijze waarop de aanbieders, gebruikers en abonnees voorlichten over het gebruik van nummeridentificatie.

verdict.shared_actor: The minister responsible for issuing ministerial regulations (the competent rule-making authority), insofar as both provisions confer competence on that authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: A ministerial regulation is being considered in the relevant digital-law context. Norm A concerns the use of public identification means and the facilities referred to in Article 5(1); Norm B concerns necessary data sharing between the ACM and the competent authorities for implementing the Act.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires rules to be established by ministerial regulation concerning the use of public identification means and the facilities referred to in Article 5(1).
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B permits rules to be established by ministerial regulation concerning the provision of data between the ACM and the competent authorities referred to in paragraph 1, where necessary for implementing the Act.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a particular ministerial regulation may cover both subject matters, nor do they define the precise scope of the Article 5(1) facilities or the data-sharing conditions. Those issues do not establish mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both provisions concern ministerial rule-making, but they address different subject matters and do not require incompatible conduct. Norm A uses mandatory rule-making language ('worden regels gesteld'), while Norm B grants permissive competence ('kunnen regels worden gesteld'); exercising the latter competence does not prevent compliance with the former.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling worden regels gesteld met betrekking tot het gebruik van publieke identificatiemiddelen en de voorzieningen, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij ministeriële regeling kunnen regels worden gesteld over het verstrekken van gegevens tussen de Autoriteit Consument en Markt en de bevoegde autoriteiten, bedoeld in het eerste lid, die noodzakelijk zijn voor de uitvoering van deze wet.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the applicant for recognition of a bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel or associated services; however, Norm A specifically addresses the user of an admitted identification means, so the texts do not establish that the same actor necessarily falls under both rules.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap only if the applicant under Norm B is also a user of an admitted identification means under Norm A. Norm B applies when applying for recognition; Norm A has no stated trigger beyond use of the admitted identification means.
verdict.requirement_a: The user of an admitted identification means must take all necessary measures to prevent misuse, theft, loss, or dissemination of that identification means.
verdict.requirement_b: When applying for recognition, a certificate of conformity must in any event be provided, issued by a conformity-assessment body designated by the Minister.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether the recognition applicant is also the user covered by Norm A, nor whether the required security measures affect the certificate requirement. No mutually exclusive duty or express reconciliation is stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different subject matter and are jointly performable: security measures for an identification means and provision of a conformity certificate. Similarity of actor or context does not make them contradictory.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel neemt alle nodige maatregelen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij de aanvraag om erkenning wordt in elk geval een certificaat van conformiteit verstrekt, die is afgegeven door een door Onze Minister aan te wijzen conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstantie.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly shared actor: Norm A applies to the user of an admitted identification means; Norm B concerns the competent authority or government in relation to an algemene maatregel van bestuur and parliamentary chambers.
verdict.shared_circumstance: At most, both concern conduct under the same statute; the provisions do not establish the same triggering situation or overlapping regulated act.
verdict.requirement_a: The user of an admitted identification means must take all necessary measures to prevent misuse, theft, loss, or dissemination of that identification means.
verdict.requirement_b: An algemene maatregel van bestuur established under Article 5(6) must be submitted to both Houses of Parliament, with its entry into force subject to the stated four-week procedure and exceptions.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction: the norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger, and compliance with one does not prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel neemt alle nodige maatregelen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een krachtens artikel 5, zesde lid, vastgestelde algemene maatregel van bestuur wordt aan beide Kamers der Staten-Generaal overgelegd.

verdict.shared_actor: Geen gedeelde actor vastgesteld: Norm A richt zich tot de gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel; Norm B tot een bestuursorgaan of aangewezen organisatie.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Er is geen voldoende specifieke gedeelde trigger. Norm A geldt bij gebruik van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel; Norm B betreft het tijdstip waarop acceptatieplichten van toepassing worden na aansluiting volgens een aansluitschema.
verdict.requirement_a: De gebruiker moet alle nodige maatregelen nemen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.requirement_b: De acceptatieplichten van artikelen 7 en 15 zijn voor een bestuursorgaan of aangewezen organisatie niet eerder van toepassing dan nadat aansluiting op de infrastructuur en voorzieningen mogelijk is volgens het aansluitschema.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Niet vastgesteld is of een bestuursorgaan of aangewezen organisatie in een concreet geval ook ‘gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel’ is. Zelfs bij mogelijke overlap verbiedt Norm B geen beveiligingsmaatregelen en verplicht Norm A niet tot eerdere aanvaarding; de bepalingen kunnen dus naast elkaar worden nageleefd.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen wederzijds onverenigbare plichten op aan dezelfde actor voor dezelfde trigger. Norm B bevat bovendien een temporele beperking van acceptatieplichten, niet een verbod op de maatregelen uit Norm A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel neemt alle nodige maatregelen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in de artikelen 7 en 15 opgenomen acceptatieplichten zijn voor een bestuursorgaan of aangewezen organisatie niet eerder van toepassing dan nadat dat bestuursorgaan of die aangewezen organisatie kan worden aangesloten op de in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdelen a tot en met e, en tweede lid bedoelde infrastructuur en voorzieningen overeenkomstig het bij regeling van Onze Minister, gehoord Onze Ministers die het mede aangaat, op te stellen aansluitschema.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially, a user of an authorised identification means under Norm A who also uses a real-time remote biometric identification system in public spaces for law-enforcement purposes under Norm B.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Only where that actor's identification means and the real-time remote biometric-identification use are involved in the same operational context. Norm A applies to preventing misuse, theft, loss or dissemination of the identification means; Norm B applies to the specified law-enforcement use in public spaces.
verdict.requirement_a: The user must take all necessary measures to prevent misuse, theft, loss or dissemination of their identification means.
verdict.requirement_b: The use of the real-time remote biometric-identification system must be subject to prior authorisation by a judicial or independent administrative authority, subject to the stated emergency exception and subsequent application deadline.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not establish that the identification means in Norm A is the biometric-identification system in Norm B, nor do they specify how the security measures under Norm A interact with the authorisation procedure under Norm B. Norm B's emergency exception and the consequences of refusal remain relevant to any concrete application.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different, compatible duties: security measures to prevent misuse of an identification means and an authorisation requirement for a specified biometric-identification use. Neither provision requires conduct that the other forbids, and joint compliance is possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel neemt alle nodige maatregelen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor de toepassing van lid 1, eerste alinea, punt h), en lid 2, wordt elk gebruik van systemen voor biometrische identificatie op afstand in real time in openbare ruimten met het oog op de rechtshandhaving afhankelijk gesteld van een voorafgaande toestemming die wordt verleend door een gerechtelijke instantie of een onafhankelijke administratieve instantie

verdict.shared_actor: A user of an authorised identification means who is also the user/operator responsible for a high-risk AI system covered by Annex III, point 1(a)
verdict.shared_circumstance: The actor uses the identification means in connection with a covered high-risk AI system and faces risks of misuse, theft, loss or dissemination while the system produces an identification on which action or a decision might be based.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the user to take all necessary measures to prevent misuse, theft, loss or dissemination of the identification means.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits the responsible user from taking measures or making decisions based on the system's identification unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two qualified, trained and authorised natural persons. The separate-verification requirement has an express proportionality exception for certain law-enforcement, migration, border-control and asylum uses.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether a particular preventive measure under Norm A would itself constitute a measure or decision based on the AI system's identification, nor whether the actor and factual circumstances fall within Norm B's scope or its sectoral exception. On the stated facts, the duties can be performed together: preventive security measures can be taken while any AI-based measure or decision is made only after the required verification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties. Norm A requires preventive security measures concerning the identification means; Norm B restricts reliance on a high-risk AI identification for measures or decisions, subject to verification. Joint compliance is plausibly possible, and no provision requires what the other forbids.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De gebruiker van een toegelaten identificatiemiddel neemt alle nodige maatregelen om misbruik, diefstal, verlies of verspreiding van zijn identificatiemiddel te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor AI-systemen met een hoog risico als bedoeld in bijlage III, punt 1, a), zijn de maatregelen als bedoeld in lid 3 van dit artikel zodanig dat zij waarborgen dat daarnaast door de gebruiksverantwoordelijke geen maatregelen worden getroffen of beslissingen worden genomen op basis van de identificatie door het systeem, tenzij deze identificatie door ten minste twee natuurlijke personen met de nodige bekwaamheid, opleiding en bevoegdheid apart zijn geverifieerd en bevestigd.

verdict.shared_actor: The competent public authority or ministerial body: Norm A concerns the authority granting an accreditation; Norm B concerns the authority making the proposal for the specified general administrative measure.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both could concern governmental action under BWBR0048156, but the provisions do not establish the same concrete triggering situation. Norm A concerns granting an accreditation for a business or organisational means and associated services; Norm B concerns proposing a general administrative measure under Article 16(4).
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants a competence: conditions or limitations may be attached to an accreditation.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits making the proposal for the general administrative measure earlier than four weeks after the draft has been submitted to both Houses, subject to the stated exception where a legislative wish is expressed within that period.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether the authority exercising the accreditation competence is also the authority making the proposal under Article 25, nor do they create a situation in which attaching accreditation conditions or limitations would require making the proposal before the four-week period expires. The exception in Norm B is therefore not material to any demonstrated conflict.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction is established: the norms regulate different governmental acts, and nothing in the text makes exercising the competence in Norm A incompatible with complying with Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aan een erkenning kunnen voorschriften of beperkingen worden verbonden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De voordracht voor een krachtens artikel 16, vierde lid, vast te stellen algemene maatregel van bestuur wordt niet eerder gedaan dan vier weken nadat het ontwerp aan beide kamers der Staten-Generaal is overgelegd, tenzij binnen deze termijn door of namens een van de Kamers of door ten minste een vijfde van het grondwettelijk aantal leden van een van de Kamers de wens te kennen wordt gegeven het onderwerp van de algemene maatregel van bestuur bij wet te regelen.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: An application for recognition of an authentication service/business-and-organisation means, where the service satisfies the applicable rules and there is also a serious danger that recognition would be used for criminal offences, criminal proceeds, or would otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_a: The Minister must refuse the application when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including when such a serious danger exists.
verdict.requirement_b: The Minister must recognise the authentication service at the requested assurance level if it satisfies the rules set for that level by or under a general administrative measure.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not expressly state whether the serious-danger refusal ground overrides the otherwise applicable duty to recognise a compliant service, or whether compliance with the prescribed rules excludes that danger. The provisions can plausibly be reconciled by treating the refusal ground as an overriding exception to the recognition duty, but that priority is not explicit in the quoted text.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms address the same decision by the same actor, but the text does not establish that their conditions necessarily coincide or that the duties are mutually exclusive. A plausible reconciliation exists, so contradiction is not proven; the unresolved relationship between the refusal ground and the conditional recognition duty prevents a firm non-conflict conclusion.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: An application or service is being considered for recognition under Article 11; the provisions do not establish that both conditions necessarily occur in the same case.
verdict.requirement_a: Refuse an application for recognition when serious danger exists that recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Recognize an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst when the service complies with rules established by or pursuant to an algemene maatregel van bestuur.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a service satisfying the applicable administrative rules under Norm B can also present the serious danger described in Norm A, and how the provisions are ordered or reconciled in that overlap. The text does not expressly state that compliance with the administrative rules overrides the refusal ground, or vice versa.
verdict.criterion_fired: The same actor and broadly related recognition context are present, but the provisions have different triggers and the supplied text does not establish that both triggers apply simultaneously. Nor does it show that recognition is required despite the refusal condition. Therefore a contradiction cannot be established.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's handling of decisions under the electronic-services recognition/attribute-designation framework, but Article 11 applies specifically when serious danger exists; Article 12 states an unconditional publication duty for a designation decision.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must refuse an application for recognition when serious danger exists that the recognition will be used for criminal offences, criminal proceeds, or will otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 12, the Minister must announce a decision designating attributes in the Staatscourant.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions concern different decisions: refusal of a recognition application versus announcement of an attribute-designation decision. The text does not establish that an attribute-designation decision is necessarily a recognition decision or that publication is required for a refused recognition application.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not mutually exclusive: refusing a recognition application and publishing an attribute-designation decision can both be performed, and the provisions do not require opposite actions for the same decision and trigger.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Van een besluit tot aanwijzing doet Onze Minister mededeling in de Staatscourant.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the Minister responsible for recognition and directions concerning recognized services)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's regulation of electronic-service recognition or recognized services in the context of reliable and secure electronic service access. However, the specific triggers differ: serious danger to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-service system under Article 11, versus the Minister's judgment that binding directions are necessary for reliable access under Article 13.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons exist, including a serious danger that the recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-service system.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 13, the Minister may give binding directions to a recognized service when, in the Minister's judgment, this is necessary for reliable access by enterprises and legal entities to electronic services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a service affected by an Article 11 refusal could also be subject to Article 13 directions, nor do they detail how any implementing rules under Article 13 interact with the refusal ground in Article 11. This does not establish mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules do not impose contradictory duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Article 11 requires refusal of an application in specified danger circumstances, while Article 13 grants a discretionary competence to issue binding directions to an already recognized service in a different circumstance. The Minister could comply with both by refusing a dangerous application and, where necessary, issuing directions to an existing recognized service.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern ministerial action relating to electronic-service recognition or recognized services, but their triggers differ: serious danger to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system under Norm A, versus rules obstructing technological developments concerning reliable access under Norm B.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the Minister to refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons exist, including a serious danger that the recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B authorizes, but does not require, the Minister to grant an exemption from rules under or pursuant to Article 13 when those rules obstruct technological developments concerning reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify whether an exemption under Norm B could ever concern rules relevant to a pending recognition application or override the refusal duty in Norm A. However, Norm B is discretionary and does not expressly require granting an exemption, so no incompatibility is established.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties for the same trigger. Norm A contains a mandatory refusal duty; Norm B grants a discretionary exemption competence under a different circumstance. Both could be complied with, including by refusing recognition under Norm A and declining to grant an exemption under Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: A recognition application or existing recognition is associated with serious reasons under Article 11—particularly a serious risk of criminal misuse, use of criminal proceeds, or danger to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including the specified serious-danger circumstances.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 14, the Minister may withdraw or suspend an existing recognition when the requirements of Article 11 or other listed requirements are not met, or when compelling reasons as referred to in Article 11(8) exist.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how the Minister should proceed if an Article 14 withdrawal or suspension decision is considered while an application under Article 11 is also pending. Article 14 expressly grants a discretionary competence ('kan'), whereas Article 11 imposes a refusal duty; the text does not make those duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules address related serious-risk circumstances and the same ministerial actor, but they govern different procedural situations and prescribe compatible responses: refusal of a pending application under Article 11 and optional withdrawal or suspension of an existing recognition under Article 14. Article 14 also refers back to Article 11 rather than requiring the Minister to grant recognition despite Article 11's refusal duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the competent minister)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern ministerial decisions affecting recognition or an electronic-service provider's activities in the electronic-services access system. However, the specific triggers differ: Article 11 concerns a serious danger justifying refusal of recognition, while Article 14 concerns withdrawal on request and a need to safeguard continuity.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must refuse an application for recognition when serious reasons exist, including a serious danger that recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use of criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 14, simultaneously with a decision to withdraw recognition on request, the Minister may impose on the service the obligation to continue its activities for a period determined by the Minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access for enterprises and legal persons.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how to handle a case in which the Article 11 security danger and the Article 14 continuity need are both present, nor whether the Article 14 continuation power could be used after or alongside a refusal decision. That uncertainty does not establish mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules do not impose incompatible duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Article 11 requires refusal of an application; Article 14 grants a discretionary power to impose temporary continuation after withdrawal on request. Their actions and conditions can be distinguished and jointly complied with.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's decision-making regarding business or organizational means used for electronic services, but they apply to different decision triggers: a serious danger opposing recognition under Article 11, versus a desired alternative means for a specific target group under Article 15.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons exist, including a serious danger that recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use of criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 15, the Minister may designate a non-recognized business or organizational means for a specified period when, for electronic services provided by a public authority or designated organization to a specific target group, use of another means is desirable due to the nature of the service or the target group's business or profession.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not expressly state how Article 15 operates if the alternative means itself presents the serious danger described in Article 11, nor whether Article 15 designation is subject to a separate recognition or security assessment. That unresolved issue does not establish a contradiction because Article 15 confers a discretionary competence and does not require designation in the Article 11 circumstances.
verdict.criterion_fired: The same actor may be involved, but the rules do not impose mutually exclusive duties for the same trigger: Article 11 requires refusal of recognition upon serious danger, while Article 15 permits—not requires—the designation of another means under different circumstances. Joint compliance is therefore possible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Overheidsorganen op Rijksniveau, bestuursorganen op Rijksniveau en aangewezen organisaties could be competent under Norm B; Onze Minister is the actor under Norm A. The texts do not establish that these are the same actor.
verdict.shared_circumstance: There is no expressly shared trigger. Norm A applies when serious danger exists that recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system. Norm B concerns supervision of compliance with specified provisions.
verdict.requirement_a: Onze Minister must refuse an application for recognition when serious reasons oppose recognition, including the stated serious-danger circumstances.
verdict.requirement_b: The designated officials and bodies are entrusted with supervising compliance with the provisions listed in Article 17.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether any actor competent to supervise under Article 17 is also the Minister deciding the recognition application, and whether the supervision concerns the specific recognition decision under Article 11. Nothing in the quoted text makes the supervisory competence incompatible with the refusal duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A requires a refusal decision by the Minister; Norm B grants supervisory competence to designated authorities and organizations. Both could operate simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister and the officials designated by Our Minister, but the provisions assign different functions rather than the same duty to the same actor
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions may concern the same electronic-service recognition regime, but Article 17 applies to supervision of compliance with Articles 4 and 8, while Article 11 applies when an application for recognition presents a serious danger of criminal misuse or harm to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 11 requires Our Minister to refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons oppose recognition, including when there is a serious danger of criminal misuse or harm to the system's reliability and security.

verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: An application for recognition under Article 11 is being processed, potentially in circumstances where serious danger exists to the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 11 requires the Minister to refuse an application for recognition when compelling reasons exist, including serious danger that the recognition will facilitate criminal offences, use criminal proceeds, or otherwise endanger the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 22 authorizes, but does not require, the Minister to impose a cost-recovery levy at a tariff set by the Minister for processing an application for recognition under Article 11.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose different, compatible consequences: refusal of the application under Article 11 and optional charging of a fee for processing the application under Article 22. Article 22 does not require recognition or prohibit refusal, so both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten. Van dergelijke redenen is sprake in geval ernstig gevaar bestaat dat de erkenning mede zal worden gebruikt om strafbare feiten te plegen of uit strafbare feiten verkregen of te verkrijgen voordelen te benutten of anderszins de betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van het Nederlandse stelsel voor elektronische dienstverlening in gevaar komt.

verdict.shared_actor: Een bevoegde overheidsautoriteit: de Nederlandse minister onder norm A en een aanmeldende autoriteit onder norm B; alleen indien dezelfde autoriteit in de concrete context beide bevoegdheden heeft, kunnen beide normen op één actor rusten.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Er bestaat een probleem met de betrouwbaarheid, veiligheid of rechtmatigheid van een elektronische-dienstverlener of aangemelde instantie: bij norm A een ernstig gevaar voor misbruik van de erkenning of aantasting van het Nederlandse stelsel, en bij norm B voldoende reden om aan te nemen dat een aangemelde instantie niet meer aan de eisen voldoet of haar verplichtingen niet nakomt.
verdict.requirement_a: De minister moet de aanvraag tot erkenning weigeren wanneer zwaarwegende redenen, waaronder het omschreven ernstige gevaar, zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.requirement_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit moet de kwestie onverwijld en zo zorgvuldig mogelijk onderzoeken; na de vereiste conclusie moet zij, indien passend en afhankelijk van de ernst, de aanwijzing beperken, schorsen of intrekken en de Commissie en andere lidstaten informeren.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Niet vaststaat of dezelfde autoriteit, dezelfde instantie en exact dezelfde procedurele situatie onder beide bepalingen vallen. Ook is niet uitgewerkt hoe een eventuele weigering van erkenning zich verhoudt tot beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een aanwijzing. Die institutionele en procedurele overlap bewijst echter geen tegenstrijdigheid.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichtingen zijn niet wederzijds exclusief: norm A betreft weigering van een erkenningsaanvraag, terwijl norm B onderzoek en eventueel beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een aanwijzing voorschrijft. Beide kunnen achtereenvolgens of naast elkaar worden nageleefd; geen van beide vereist wat de andere verbiedt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister weigert een aanvraag tot erkenning, indien zwaarwegende redenen zich tegen erkenning verzetten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een aanmeldende autoriteit voldoende reden heeft om van mening te zijn dat een aangemelde instantie niet meer aan de eisen van artikel 31 voldoet of haar verplichtingen niet nakomt, moet de aanmeldende autoriteit de kwestie onverwijld zo zorgvuldig mogelijk onderzoeken.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: A service seeking recognition that satisfies the applicable rules established by or under a general administrative measure; the provisions could apply to the same minister in relation to services covered by Article 11.
verdict.requirement_a: Recognize an authentication service at the reliability level of the business or organizational means for which recognition is sought, if the service satisfies the rules applicable to that reliability level.
verdict.requirement_b: Recognize an access-enabling service or an authorization service if the service satisfies the rules applicable to that service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify whether a single service can simultaneously qualify as an authentication service and as an access-enabling or authorization service, or how overlapping classifications and applicable rules would be handled. That unresolved classification issue does not establish mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both provisions impose recognition duties on the same actor, but they concern different service categories and contain no mutually exclusive requirement or prohibition. If one service falls within both categories and satisfies both sets of rules, the Minister could recognize it under both provisions; the text does not make joint compliance impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the competent recognizing authority)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions apply when the relevant authentication service, issuer/service, and associated business/organizational means satisfy the applicable rules established by or under a general administrative measure.
verdict.requirement_a: Recognize an authentication service at the reliability level of the business or organizational means for which recognition is sought, if the service satisfies the applicable rules.
verdict.requirement_b: Recognize a means issuer in relation to a business or organizational means to be issued by that service and its associated reliability level, if the service and the means satisfy the applicable rules.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify the detailed rules or whether recognition under one provision is a prerequisite for, or otherwise affects, recognition under the other. That relationship remains unresolved, but no mutually exclusive duties appear in the text.
verdict.criterion_fired: The same authority may perform both recognition acts, and the duties concern different objects—an authentication service versus a means issuer and associated means. Nothing in either provision forbids or makes impossible the other recognition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een middelenuitgever met betrekking tot een door die dienst uit te geven bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel en het bijbehorende betrouwbaarheidsniveau, indien de dienst en het middel voldoen aan de daartoe bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's regulation of authentication services or attributes for electronic identification/services, including services at the substantial or high assurance level. However, the exact triggering conditions are not identical.
verdict.requirement_a: If an authentication service satisfies the rules set by or pursuant to an order in council for the relevant assurance level, the Minister must recognize it at the assurance level for which recognition is sought.
verdict.requirement_b: The Minister may designate an attribute that, in the Minister's opinion, is important for identifying enterprises or legal persons under Article 15(1), for certain electronic services at the substantial or high level, and that must consequently be used by services recognized under Article 11.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how a designated attribute interacts with the detailed recognition requirements established by or pursuant to an order in council. It is unresolved whether any particular attribute requirement could affect compliance with those requirements, but no incompatibility is stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different, compatible functions: Article 11 requires recognition when its conditions are met, while Article 12 grants a power to designate attributes and makes their use applicable to recognized services. Neither provision requires what the other forbids, and Article 12 does not negate or prevent recognition under Article 11.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan een attribuut aanwijzen dat naar zijn oordeel van belang is voor de identificatie van ondernemingen of rechtspersonen als bedoeld in artikel 15, eerste lid, ten behoeve van bepaalde elektronische dienstverlening op het niveau substantieel of hoog en daartoe door de op grond van artikel 11 erkende diensten moeten worden gehanteerd.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern a ministerial decision in the digital-law domain, but their specific triggers differ: Norm A applies when an authentication service seeks recognition at a specified assurance level and satisfies the applicable rules; Norm B applies when an attribute is included in a register based on a statutory provision.
verdict.requirement_a: Under the applicable assurance-level rules, Onze Minister must recognize an authentication service at the assurance level for which recognition is sought, provided the service complies with the rules set by or under a general administrative measure.
verdict.requirement_b: If an attribute is included in a register based on a statutory provision, Onze Minister must decide on the designation of that attribute in agreement with the minister concerned.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how to coordinate the decisions if the same ministerial act were somehow subject to both procedures, nor do they identify the minister concerned under Norm B. Nothing in the text makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose distinct, potentially cumulative duties triggered by different circumstances. Neither requires an act that the other forbids, and both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een attribuut is opgenomen in een register, dat berust op een wettelijk voorschrift, neemt Onze Minister het besluit tot aanwijzing van dat attribuut in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het mede aangaat.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister's regulation of authentication/recognized services in the context of reliable electronic access, but their precise triggers differ: Article 11 applies when an authentication service meets the applicable reliability-level rules; Article 13 applies when the Minister considers binding directions necessary for reliable access.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 11 requires the Minister to recognize an authentication service at the requested reliability level if the service satisfies the rules established for that level.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 13 gives the Minister the competence to issue binding directions to a recognized service when, in the Minister's opinion, this is necessary for reliable access by enterprises and legal entities to electronic services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provision does not specify the content or limits of any binding directions, nor how they interact with the recognition requirements. Nothing in the text indicates that issuing directions would prevent or contradict recognition under Article 11.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties. Article 11 concerns mandatory recognition upon satisfaction of applicable requirements, while Article 13 grants a discretionary power to issue binding directions to an already recognized service; both can operate together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien dit naar zijn oordeel voor een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening noodzakelijk is, kan Onze Minister een erkende dienst bindende aanwijzingen geven.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister and the erkende diensten within the statutory scheme
verdict.shared_circumstance: The recognition of an authentication service and the subsequent or related regulation of recognized services under the same statutory framework; however, the provisions do not establish an identical concrete trigger for both rules.
verdict.requirement_a: Onze Minister must recognize an authentication service at the requested reliability level if the service satisfies the rules prescribed for that level by or under a general administrative measure.
verdict.requirement_b: Rules may be established by or under a general administrative measure concerning disclosure/cooperation and cooperation between recognized services.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify the content of the possible rules under Article 13 or how they interact with the recognition criteria under Article 11. No provision shown requires Article 13 rules to conflict with recognition or makes compliance with one impossible while complying with the other.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different kinds of legal effects—conditional recognition under Article 11 and legislative/regulatory competence under Article 13—and nothing in the supplied text makes their simultaneous operation or compliance impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een authenticatiedienst op het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel waarvoor hij erkend wenst te worden, indien de dienst voldoet aan de daartoe voor dat betrouwbaarheidsniveau bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen regels worden gesteld over de ontsluiting en medewerking, bedoeld in het derde lid en over de samenwerking tussen de erkende diensten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: An authentication/recognized service is involved, and the applicable statutory or regulatory rules concern reliable electronic access by enterprises and legal entities. However, the provisions do not establish that the exact same factual trigger necessarily activates both rules.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A requires the Minister to recognize an authentication service at the requested assurance level if the service satisfies the rules set for that assurance level by or under a general administrative order.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives the Minister the competence to grant an exemption to a recognized service from rules established by or under Article 13 when those rules obstruct technological developments concerning reliable access to electronic services.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister acting within the framework of this Act, but they apply to different operational situations: recognition of a service under Article 11 versus provision of information about a breach under Article 19 when necessary for specified tasks or services.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must recognize an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst if that service satisfies the rules established by or pursuant to a general administrative order.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 19, the Minister must provide data and information about an infringement of secure and reliable access to electronic services to the listed recipients, insofar as necessary for the proper performance of their tasks or services under the Act.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether particular information may be withheld or how Article 19 interacts with confidentiality, data-protection, or other statutory restrictions. That issue is unresolved, but no textual incompatibility between the duties is shown.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not mutually exclusive: recognizing a qualifying service and providing necessary information about an access infringement can both be performed. Neither provision requires the Minister to do what the other forbids, and neither provision expressly defers to or overrides the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: The Minister acts under the same statute, but the provisions do not establish the same triggering circumstances: Article 11 concerns recognition of an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst when it meets rules set by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur; Article 21 concerns charging costs incurred in implementing Articles 5 and 9 to the relevant bodies.
verdict.requirement_a: Under Article 11, the Minister must recognize an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst if the service satisfies the applicable rules set by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur.
verdict.requirement_b: Under Article 21, the Minister must charge costs incurred by the State in connection with implementing Articles 5 and 9 to the relevant administrative bodies, designated organizations, and other relevant bodies, subject to further rules by ministerial regulation.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether recognition under Article 11 could generate costs covered by Article 21, nor do they define the relationship between the cost-charging mechanism and recognition decisions. That omission does not make the duties mutually exclusive.
