verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction would require a specific fact or applicable rule showing that exercising the Article 13 exemption necessarily requires the same actor to disclose Article 78 information that Article 28 requires it to keep confidential, with no lawful restricted-disclosure or other reconciliation available.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger: Norm A grants ministerial discretion, while Norm B imposes a confidentiality obligation, and the text contains no requirement that the exemption involve disclosure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van bij of krachtens artikel 13 gestelde regels, indien deze regels in de weg staan aan technologische ontwikkelingen aangaande een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: Geen duidelijk gedeelde actor: norm A betreft een erkende dienst, terwijl norm B aanmeldende autoriteiten betreft.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Hoogstens gedeeltelijk overlappende context van elektronische dienstverlening of informatieverwerking; de teksten leggen geen gemeenschappelijke trigger vast.
verdict.requirement_a: De Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van regels die bij of krachtens artikel 13 zijn gesteld wanneer die regels technologische ontwikkelingen inzake betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening belemmeren. Dit is een bevoegdheid, geen plicht voor de erkende dienst.
verdict.requirement_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten moeten waarborgen dat informatie die zij overeenkomstig artikel 78 hebben verkregen vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.
verdict.compliant_alternative: Indien één actor in een concreet geval beide hoedanigheden heeft, kan die actor de informatie vertrouwelijk behandelen en de eventuele ontheffingsbevoegdheid afzonderlijk en binnen de toepasselijke regels uitoefenen. Een ontheffing hoeft geen openbaarmaking van vertrouwelijke informatie te vereisen; zo nodig kan een verzoek of besluit worden beperkt tot niet-vertrouwelijke, geanonimiseerde of anderszins rechtmatig te delen informatie.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Niet duidelijk is welke regels precies 'bij of krachtens artikel 13' zijn bedoeld, of artikel 78 uitzonderingen op vertrouwelijkheid bevat, en of een erkende dienst tevens een aanmeldende autoriteit kan zijn. Ook is niet vastgesteld dat een ontheffing openbaarmaking of een andere handeling vereist die met vertrouwelijkheid strijdt.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: De uitkomst zou kunnen veranderen als een toepasselijke regel of een concreet ontheffingsbesluit uitdrukkelijk vereist dat overeenkomstig artikel 78 verkregen informatie openbaar wordt gemaakt of anderszins wordt gebruikt op een wijze die vertrouwelijke behandeling onmogelijk maakt, zonder beperkte of geanonimiseerde nalevingsmogelijkheid.
verdict.criterion_fired: Geen tegenstrijdige verplichtingen vastgesteld: norm A verleent een discretionaire bevoegdheid aan de Minister en norm B legt een vertrouwelijkheidsverplichting op aan aanmeldende autoriteiten. De bepalingen hebben bovendien niet aantoonbaar dezelfde actor of trigger.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van bij of krachtens artikel 13 gestelde regels, indien deze regels in de weg staan aan technologische ontwikkelingen aangaande een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an actor that is both an erkende dienst under BWBR0048156 and a nationale bevoegde autoriteit under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; the provisions do not establish that these categories actually overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The overlap would arise only if such an actor performs tasks as a national competent authority while the rules under Article 13 obstruct technological developments concerning reliable access to electronic services. Norm B otherwise has no stated triggering condition.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence to grant an erkende dienst an exemption from rules laid down by or under Article 13 when those rules obstruct relevant technological developments. It does not itself impose a duty on the erkende dienst.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges national competent authorities, when performing their tasks, to comply with the confidentiality obligations laid down in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister could grant an exemption under Norm A only to the extent permitted by the applicable exemption framework, while the actor continues to comply with Article 78 confidentiality obligations—for example, by using a restricted-access, anonymised, or otherwise confidentiality-preserving form of the relevant technological development. Norm A does not require disclosure or non-confidential conduct.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish whether any particular erkende dienst is also a national competent authority, what Article 13 rules might be exempted, or whether a requested exemption could lawfully affect Article 78 confidentiality duties. Article 70 itself does not state an exception or priority rule.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if a specific Article 13 rule or exemption decision required the same actor, for the same task and circumstances, to disclose or use information in a manner that Article 78 absolutely forbids, with no restricted, anonymised, phased, or other compliant alternative. Conversely, proof that the actor categories do not overlap would eliminate any shared-actor issue.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties: Norm A confers discretionary exemption competence on the Minister, whereas Norm B imposes confidentiality compliance on national competent authorities. The text supplies no requirement that an exemption breach or override confidentiality obligations.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van bij of krachtens artikel 13 gestelde regels, indien deze regels in de weg staan aan technologische ontwikkelingen aangaande een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij de uitvoering van hun taken voldoen de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten aan de in artikel 78 vastgelegde vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: An erkende dienst (recognised service) under BWBR0048156, and, for Norm B, the government authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, but the texts do not establish that these are the same actors.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap only if a recognised service is also one of the Article 77(1) authorities or bodies and has obtained information or documentation under Article 77 while the Article 13 rules obstruct technological developments concerning reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_a: The Minister may grant a recognised service an exemption from rules laid down by or under Article 13 when those rules obstruct relevant technological developments. This is a discretionary competence, not an unconditional duty on the recognised service.
verdict.requirement_b: Information or documentation obtained under Article 77 by the authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) must be processed in accordance with the confidentiality obligations in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The authority or body can process the information in accordance with Article 78 while the recognised service continues complying with the Article 13 rules. If those rules obstruct the relevant technological development, the Minister may grant an exemption; that exemption does not require disclosure or processing contrary to Article 78.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether a recognised service can also be an Article 77(1) authority or body, what the Article 13 rules are, or the content of Article 78's confidentiality obligations. The scope and conditions of any exemption therefore remain unresolved.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become possible only if the missing Article 78 obligations expressly required the same actor to disclose or process information in a manner that an applicable Article 13 rule absolutely prohibited, with no lawful exemption or restricted-processing alternative. Conversely, confirmation that the actors cannot overlap would eliminate even a potential shared-actor scenario.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A grants a conditional ministerial exemption competence, while Norm B imposes a confidentiality-compliant processing obligation; the text supplies no incompatibility.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van bij of krachtens artikel 13 gestelde regels, indien deze regels in de weg staan aan technologische ontwikkelingen aangaande een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly shared actor is established. Norm A concerns the Minister's competence to grant an exemption to an erkende dienst; Norm B concerns national public authorities or bodies supervising or enforcing fundamental-rights obligations regarding high-risk AI systems.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern regulated digital-service activity and public-authority oversight, but the provisions do not establish the same triggering situation. Norm A applies when rules hinder technological developments concerning reliable access to electronic services. Norm B applies when access to documentation is needed for effective exercise of a supervisory or enforcement mandate concerning listed high-risk AI systems.
verdict.requirement_a: The Minister may grant an erkende dienst an exemption from rules laid down by or under Article 13 if those rules obstruct relevant technological developments.
verdict.requirement_b: A competent national fundamental-rights authority or body may request and inspect documentation prepared or maintained under the AI Act, in an accessible language and format, when access is needed for effective exercise of its mandate within its jurisdiction; it must notify the market-surveillance authority of the request.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The provisions can be complied with simultaneously because Norm A grants a discretionary exemption competence, while Norm B grants an information-access competence to a different category of authority. If an exempted erkende dienst also falls within the AI-documentation regime, the authorities can provide or inspect the requested documentation in the required accessible form while the Minister separately decides any exemption request; no disclosure prohibition or mandatory exemption is stated.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether an exemption under Article 13 could cover, alter, or limit documentation duties under the AI Act, nor whether the same institution could hold both roles. Any applicable confidentiality, data-protection, or sector-specific limitation is not provided.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if another applicable provision made the Article 13 exemption require withholding or preventing access to documentation that Norm B unconditionally requires the authority to provide or inspect, with no lawful redaction, anonymisation, delayed-access, or other accommodation. The identity of the Minister and authorities, and whether the erkende dienst operates a listed high-risk AI system, would also determine whether both norms apply in practice.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. They confer separate competences on different actors, and the text contains no prohibition preventing simultaneous exercise.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkende dienst ontheffing verlenen van bij of krachtens artikel 13 gestelde regels, indien deze regels in de weg staan aan technologische ontwikkelingen aangaande een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen die de nakoming van verplichtingen krachtens Unierecht ter bescherming van grondrechten, waaronder het recht op non-discriminatie, met betrekking tot het gebruik van de in bijlage III vermelde AI-systemen met een hoog risico controleren of handhaven, zijn bevoegd om krachtens deze verordening opgestelde of bijgehouden documentatie in een toegankelijke taal en een toegankelijk formaat aan te vragen en in te zien wanneer toegang tot die documentatie nodig is voor het doeltreffend uitoefenen van de bevoegdheden onder hun mandaat binnen de grenzen van hun rechtsgebied.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern a decision under Article 14, although Norm A applies when the specified non-compliance or serious reasons exist, while Norm B applies to a decision referred to in the article.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence to withdraw or suspend an accreditation, and possibly to impose an obligation to prepare a termination plan simultaneously with withdrawal.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges Onze Minister to announce a decision referred to in Article 14 in the Staatscourant.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify whether every withdrawal or suspension decision under Norm A is necessarily a decision covered by Norm B, but nothing in the provisions makes the competence to withdraw or suspend incompatible with the publication obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different, compatible requirements: a discretionary competence to withdraw or suspend an accreditation and a publication obligation concerning an Article 14 decision. The Minister can exercise the competence and also publish the decision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Van een besluit als bedoeld in dit artikel doet Onze Minister mededeling in de Staatscourant.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister, in relation to the betrokken dienst and an accreditation/recognition decision
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern a decision to withdraw an erkenning; Norm B specifically concerns withdrawal on request, while Norm A concerns withdrawal or suspension for non-compliance or serious reasons. The texts do not establish that these triggers necessarily coincide.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence to withdraw an erkenning or suspend it for a specified period when the listed non-compliance or serious-reason conditions apply, and, simultaneously with withdrawal, to impose an obligation to prepare a termination plan.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives Onze Minister the competence, simultaneously with a withdrawal on request, to require the betrokken dienst to continue its activities providing access to electronic services for a period determined by the Minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a withdrawal on request can also occur under the conditions in Norm A and, if so, whether the termination-plan obligation and the continuation obligation would create any practical incompatibility. The text does not make the obligations mutually exclusive; both could plausibly be imposed together.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions confer potentially concurrent competences and obligations, but neither requires conduct that the other forbids. Joint compliance is possible, and Norm B's continuation period can coexist with a termination plan.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Gelijktijdig met een besluit tot intrekking, kan Onze Minister de betrokken dienst de verplichting opleggen tot het opstellen van een beëindigingplan als bedoeld in het eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gelijktijdig met een besluit tot intrekking op verzoek kan Onze Minister de betrokken dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister / the deciding authority under the scheme
verdict.shared_circumstance: A decision concerns an accreditation or a business/organizational means in circumstances where the applicable statutory requirements may not be met. The texts do not establish that both provisions govern the same decision or trigger.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A grants the Minister competence to withdraw or suspend an accreditation when specified requirements, conditions, binding instructions, or serious-reason grounds are not satisfied.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits taking a decision referred to in Article 15(5) concerning a business or organizational means that fails the security and reliability requirements for the substantial or high assurance level.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It remains unresolved whether the Article 15(5) decision is the same type of decision as the withdrawal or suspension decision under Article 14, and whether the relevant accreditation and business/organizational means are legally identical. If they are distinct, both rules can plainly be complied with; even if related, Norm A confers a power rather than requiring the Minister to take an incompatible decision.
verdict.criterion_fired: No contradiction is established: Norm A is a discretionary competence to withdraw or suspend an accreditation, while Norm B prohibits a particular decision concerning a non-compliant business or organizational means. The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger, and joint compliance is plausible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een besluit als bedoeld in het vijfde lid wordt niet genomen ten aanzien van een bedrijfs- of organisatiemiddel dat niet voldoet aan de voor het betrouwbaarheidsniveau substantieel of hoog gestelde eisen ten aanzien van veiligheid en betrouwbaarheid.

verdict.shared_actor: De Minister (voor intrekking of schorsing) and aangewezen ambtenaren / bestuursorganen / aangewezen organisaties (for toezicht)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both concern enforcement or compliance within the same statutory scheme, but the provisions specify different triggers: Norm A applies when specified requirements, conditions, or binding instructions are not complied with; Norm B applies to supervision of compliance with articles 3, 6, 7, 8(1), and 15.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence to withdraw or suspend an erkenning, and possibly impose an obligation to prepare a termination plan, when the listed non-compliance or serious reasons exist.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B assigns designated officials, administrative bodies, and designated organisations the competence/responsibility to supervise compliance with the listed provisions.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify how supervisory findings under article 17 interact with the Minister's withdrawal or suspension competence under article 14, nor whether any particular designation or procedural limitation applies. That unresolved relationship does not make the competences mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms confer different, compatible enforcement competences on different actors and do not require mutually exclusive conduct. Supervision can coexist with the Minister's discretionary power to withdraw or suspend recognition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Met het toezicht op de naleving van het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 3 door overheidsorganen op het niveau van het Rijk en van het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 6, 7, 8, eerste lid, en 15 door bestuursorganen op het niveau van het Rijk en door de aangewezen organisaties zijn belast de bij besluit van Onze Minister die het aangaat aangewezen ambtenaren.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister and the officials designated by Onze Minister (but the provisions assign different competences rather than the same duty to the same actor)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both concern enforcement or regulatory oversight under BWBR0048156, but Article 14 applies when specified obligations, conditions, restrictions, or binding instructions are not complied with, while Article 17 concerns supervision of compliance with Articles 4 and 8(2)–(3).
verdict.requirement_a: Article 14 gives Onze Minister the competence to withdraw or suspend an accreditation when the listed non-compliance or serious-reason grounds exist, and optionally to impose an obligation to prepare a termination plan upon withdrawal.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 17 assigns designated officials the competence to supervise compliance with Article 4 and Article 8(2)–(3).
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify whether the Article 17 officials may supervise matters relevant to Article 14 or how their supervisory findings interact with the Minister’s withdrawal or suspension competence. That institutional relationship is unresolved, but no mutually exclusive duties are stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions confer different, compatible enforcement competences and do not require the same actor to perform mutually exclusive acts under the same trigger. Article 14 permits withdrawal or suspension; Article 17 assigns supervision. Supervision can coexist with, and potentially inform, a later withdrawal or suspension decision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Met het toezicht op de naleving van het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 4 en het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 8, tweede en derde lid, zijn belast de bij besluit van Onze Minister aangewezen ambtenaren.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister / the competent public authority responsible for the recognition regime (potentially involved in both provisions)
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the administration of an erkenning (recognition), including circumstances involving recognition-related acts or compliance with recognition requirements. However, Article 22 specifically concerns rules on charging fees, while Article 14 concerns non-compliance or serious reasons justifying withdrawal or suspension.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 14 grants the Minister competence to withdraw or suspend a recognition when the stated recognition requirements, conditions, binding instructions, or serious-reason grounds are not satisfied; it may also impose an obligation to prepare a termination plan upon withdrawal.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 22 requires that rules be established by or pursuant to a general administrative order concerning the amount and imposition of a levy, with possible distinctions between categories of acts.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not specify how any levy rules under Article 22 interact with a particular withdrawal or suspension decision under Article 14, nor does it establish whether fee non-payment could constitute non-compliance triggering Article 14. That issue is not necessary to identify a contradiction between the provisions as quoted.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, compatible functions: Article 14 confers an enforcement competence concerning recognition status, while Article 22 requires fee-related rules to be made by general administrative order. Neither provision requires the same actor to perform an act that the other forbids, and the quoted text contains no mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur worden regels gesteld over de hoogte en het opleggen van de heffing, waarbij onderscheid kan worden gemaakt tussen verschillende categorieën handelingen als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the competent minister); the affected recognized service/provider may also be affected by the exercise of the competence in Norm A and by the continuity-plan process in Norm B.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions may be relevant to regulated digital-service continuity or recognition matters involving a recognized service/provider and continuity planning. However, Norm A is triggered by non-compliance or serious reasons, while Norm B is triggered specifically when the providers cannot agree on a joint continuity plan.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence to withdraw or suspend a recognition for a specified period when the listed non-compliance or serious-reason conditions exist, and permits imposing an obligation to prepare a termination plan simultaneously with withdrawal.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives the Minister competence to issue rules concerning the establishment of a joint continuity plan when the providers referred to in paragraph 4 cannot reach agreement on that plan.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The Minister can issue continuity-plan instructions under Norm B while separately deciding whether the conditions for withdrawal or suspension under Norm A are met. If withdrawal occurs, the affected service can prepare the required termination plan, while the other providers establish or implement the joint continuity plan. The provisions do not require the Minister to withdraw/suspend recognition and issue continuity-plan rules in mutually exclusive ways.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify how a continuity plan under Norm B interacts with a termination plan under Norm A, or whether issuing continuity-plan instructions can cure the non-compliance triggering withdrawal or suspension. They also do not identify the paragraph-4 providers or the detailed conditions in Articles 11 and 13.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if another applicable provision expressly required the Minister to maintain recognition while issuing Norm-B continuity-plan instructions, or conversely required withdrawal/suspension whenever Norm-B instructions are issued, making the duties mutually exclusive. It could also change if the full statutory scheme showed that the same provider must simultaneously remain recognized and cease operating under an unavoidable termination plan.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions confer potentially concurrent ministerial competences with different triggers and actions; neither text requires what the other forbids, and a coordinated or phased continuity/termination process is plausible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid. Gelijktijdig met een besluit tot intrekking, kan Onze Minister de betrokken dienst de verplichting opleggen tot het opstellen van een beëindigingplan als bedoeld in het eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de in het vierde lid bedoelde aanbieders geen overeenstemming kunnen bereiken over het gezamenlijke continuïteitsplan, kan Onze Minister voorschriften geven inzake het tot stand brengen van het plan.

verdict.shared_actor: De aanmeldende autoriteit kan mogelijk dezelfde overheidsautoriteit zijn als Onze Minister, voor zover die autoriteit tevens een aanwijzing of erkenning beheert.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Een beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een erkenning/aanwijzing. De teksten geven echter niet volledig aan dat beide regimes op exact dezelfde beslissing en dezelfde autoriteit zien.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A verleent Onze Minister de bevoegdheid een erkenning in te trekken of voor een bepaalde periode te schorsen wanneer de genoemde wettelijke voorschriften, voorwaarden, beperkingen of bindende aanwijzingen niet worden nageleefd, of bij zwaarwegende redenen. De minister kan daarbij ook een beëindigingsplan laten opstellen.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B verplicht de aanmeldende autoriteit, bij beperking, schorsing of intrekking van een aanwijzing, binnen drie maanden na mededeling daarvan een verslag over haar bevindingen bij de Commissie en de overige lidstaten in te dienen; daarnaast bevat de bepaling verdere maatregelen inzake certificaten.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Onzeker blijft of Onze Minister en de aanmeldende autoriteit in deze wettelijke context dezelfde actor zijn en of een erkenning onder Norm A juridisch dezelfde aanwijzing is als bedoeld in Norm B. Ook is niet duidelijk of de procedurele gevolgen van Norm B op elke intrekking of schorsing krachtens Norm A van toepassing zijn.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen onderling onverenigbare verplichtingen op. Norm A verleent een discretionaire bevoegdheid tot intrekking of schorsing; Norm B legt, indien haar trigger zich voordoet, een afzonderlijke rapportage- en opvolgingsplicht op. Die bevoegdheid kan worden uitgeoefend en de rapportageplicht kan vervolgens worden nageleefd, zodat gezamenlijke naleving plausibel is.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan een erkenning intrekken of voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode schorsen indien niet wordt voldaan aan het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 11 en 13, de aan een erkenning verbonden voorschriften of beperkingen, aan een krachtens artikel 13, vijfde lid, gegeven bindende aanwijzing of in geval van zwaarwegende redenen als bedoeld in artikel 11, achtste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient de aanmeldende autoriteit binnen drie maanden na mededeling van de wijzigingen in de aanwijzing een verslag over haar bevindingen in bij de Commissie en de overige lidstaten;

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister (the competent minister), in relation to an intended transfer of an erkenning; the requesting/recognised service may also be affected by the imposed continuation duty
verdict.shared_circumstance: A proposed transfer of an erkenning, particularly where continuity of reliable access to electronic services may be at risk. Norm A concerns the decision granting permission for transfer; Norm B governs whether permission may be granted.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence, in a transfer-permission decision, to impose on the requesting service a duty to continue its activities for a period determined by the minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires Onze Minister not to grant permission for a transfer if, in the minister's view, the transfer would or threatens to distort effective competition, or if continuity of reliable access to electronic services threatens to be jeopardised as a result of the transfer.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not expressly state how the minister must proceed when a transfer both threatens continuity and could be made continuity-safe by imposing the continuation duty. It remains unresolved whether the prohibition on granting permission applies categorically in that situation or whether permission may be granted subject to Norm A's condition. That interpretive issue does not establish an unavoidable contradiction.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A authorises a possible remedial condition when deciding on permission; Norm B prohibits permission in specified circumstances. They can be jointly complied with by refusing permission where Norm B applies, or—where legally permissible and sufficient—granting permission while imposing the continuation obligation under Norm A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verleent geen toestemming voor overdracht indien daarmee naar zijn oordeel de daadwerkelijke mededinging wordt of dreigt te worden verstoord of indien de continuïteit van een betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening met erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen als gevolg van die overdracht in het geding dreigt te komen.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister / the competent decision-maker, potentially in relation to the requesting service and a business or organisational means
verdict.shared_circumstance: A decision concerning transfer of recognition and/or a decision referred to in Article 15(5), involving electronic-identification or organisational means and the reliability/security requirements for access to electronic services. The texts do not establish that both provisions necessarily apply to the same decision or factual situation.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence, when deciding to permit a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities for a specified period insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B prohibits taking the decision referred to in Article 15(5) with respect to a business or organisational means that does not meet the security and reliability requirements for the substantial or high assurance level.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the transfer decision under Article 14 and the Article 15(5) decision concern the same actor, means, and trigger. Even if they overlap, the Article 14 competence to impose continuity obligations does not require accepting a non-compliant means, so the decision-maker can impose the continuity obligation while refraining from the prohibited acceptance decision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different, compatible legal effects: Article 14 authorises imposing a continuity obligation, while Article 15 prohibits a particular decision for means failing specified requirements. Neither rule requires what the other forbids, and the texts do not establish mutually exclusive duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een besluit als bedoeld in het vijfde lid wordt niet genomen ten aanzien van een bedrijfs- of organisatiemiddel dat niet voldoet aan de voor het betrouwbaarheidsniveau substantieel of hoog gestelde eisen ten aanzien van veiligheid en betrouwbaarheid.

verdict.shared_actor: A requesting service (de verzoekende dienst) may be subject to Norm A; a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie is subject to Norm B. The texts do not establish that these categories overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both concern access to electronic services, but Norm A applies when permission is granted for transfer of an recognition and continuity requires continued activity; Norm B applies when bestuursorganen or designated organisations provide access to their electronic services.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities in facilitating enterprises' and legal persons' access to electronic services for a specified period, insofar as necessary to ensure continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges bestuursorganen and designated organisations, when providing access to their electronic services, to accept all and only recognised business and organisational means and qualifying electronic statements, and in any event to accept one recognised ontsluitende dienst under Article 11(3).
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether a requesting service under Norm A could also qualify as a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie under Norm B, and whether any particular continued activity would involve accepting means outside Norm B's permitted category. The provisions themselves do not show such an incompatibility.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A is a ministerial competence to impose a continuity obligation; Norm B is an acceptance obligation on bestuursorganen and designated organisations. Even if an actor were subject to both, continuing access activities can plausibly be performed while accepting the means required by Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd het bepaalde in artikel 7, accepteren bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties bij de toegang tot hun elektronische dienstverlening alle en uitsluitend erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen en door erkende machtigingsdiensten afgegeven elektronische verklaringen waaruit blijkt dat een natuurlijke persoon, onderneming of rechtspersoon gemachtigd is namens de onderneming of rechtspersoon op te treden bij de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening aan die onderneming of rechtspersoon. Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties accepteren in elk geval een van de op grond van artikel 11, derde lid, erkende ontsluitende diensten.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the Minister acting under this law in circumstances involving electronic services and the exercise of statutory powers or duties; however, their specific triggers differ: Article 14 concerns approval of a transfer of recognition, while Article 19 concerns information about an infringement of secure and reliable access.
verdict.requirement_a: Article 14 gives the Minister the competence, where necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access, to impose on the requesting service a duty to continue its activities for a specified period.
verdict.requirement_b: Article 19 obliges the Minister to provide data and information to specified authorities, organizations, recognition holders, or recognized issuers/services, insofar as necessary for the proper performance of their tasks or services under the Act.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a particular transfer-approval situation under Article 14 also involves an infringement triggering Article 19, nor whether any confidentiality or other statutory restriction limits the information duty. Nothing in the quoted text makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different, compatible duties or powers on the Minister; neither requires conduct that the other forbids, and the shared subject matter is insufficient to establish a contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.shared_actor: Onze Minister, in relation to the requesting service and recognition-related procedures
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both provisions concern the statutory recognition regime and action by Onze Minister, but they apply to different immediate situations: approval of a transfer of recognition under Article 14 versus processing a recognition application or supervising compliance under Article 22.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives Onze Minister the competence, when approving a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities for a period determined by the Minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives Onze Minister the competence to impose a cost-recovery levy, according to a tariff set by him, for processing a recognition application or supervising compliance with Articles 9 and 13.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not specify whether a particular transfer approval may simultaneously involve a chargeable application or supervision activity, nor whether any separate procedural or tariff exceptions apply. That uncertainty does not make the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: Both are permissive competences concerning different measures—continuation obligations and cost-recovery levies—and neither requires or prohibits conduct incompatible with the other. The Minister could impose both where their respective conditions are met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan een heffing opleggen ter vergoeding van kosten overeenkomstig een door hem vastgesteld tarief ter zake van de volgende handelingen:

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a Dutch supervisory authority only if it is also the requesting service whose recognition is being transferred; otherwise the provisions address different actors.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The circumstances are not established as the same. Norm A concerns a decision authorising transfer of a recognition and continuity of reliable access to electronic services. Norm B concerns publication of specified certification requirements and Article 42(5) criteria by a supervisory authority.
verdict.requirement_a: Under a decision authorising transfer, the Minister may impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities providing access to electronic services for a period determined by the Minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: The supervisory authority must publish the requirements referred to in Article 43(3) and the criteria referred to in Article 42(5) in an easily accessible form, and must also communicate them to the Committee.
verdict.compliant_alternative: If the same entity could hold both roles, it could continue providing access for the Minister-specified period while separately publishing the specified certification requirements and criteria in an easily accessible form. The texts do not require disclosure of the service's operational information or prohibit continued service, so no restricted-disclosure or suspension workaround is needed.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the requesting service in Norm A can legally be the independent supervisory authority in Norm B, and whether the relevant requirements and criteria exist or fall within the stated provisions. Norm A is a competence ('may impose'), not an unconditional duty.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that the same actor is legally required by Norm B to publish information whose publication is expressly prohibited by Norm A, or that publication necessarily prevents the mandated continuation of access, could change the verdict. Conversely, confirmation that the actors are distinct would make the absence of a shared actor definitive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A grants a Minister competence to impose a continuity obligation; Norm B imposes a publication and communication obligation on a supervisory authority. Even on the hypothetical overlap of actors, both duties can be performed together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 3 van dit artikel bedoelde voorschriften en de in artikel 42, lid 5, bedoelde criteria worden door de toezichthoudende autoriteit in een eenvoudig toegankelijke vorm openbaar gemaakt. De toezichthoudende autoriteiten delen die eisen en criteria ook mee aan het Comité.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a requesting service subject to transfer of its recognition under Norm A, if it is also a member or staff member of a supervisory authority handling confidential information under Norm B; the provisions do not establish that these roles are necessarily held by the same actor.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The requesting service is involved in a transfer of recognition requiring continuity of reliable access to electronic services, while the same person is handling confidential information in the performance of supervisory-authority tasks. The texts do not expressly establish that both circumstances coincide.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, when authorising a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities for a specified period insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires members and staff of every supervisory authority to maintain professional secrecy regarding confidential information learned in performing their tasks or exercising their powers, both during and after their term; during the term this particularly covers reports of infringements by natural persons.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service could continue providing access as required by the Minister while restricting disclosure of confidential supervisory information to authorised recipients, anonymising or otherwise protecting information in any communications, and using a lawful confidential channel or fallback process. Nothing in Norm A requires disclosure of information protected by professional secrecy.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether the requesting service can simultaneously be a member or staff member of a supervisory authority, nor how professional secrecy interacts with any particular information-sharing duty arising from the continued-access obligation. No such disclosure duty is stated in Norm A.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that compliance with the Minister's continuity direction necessarily requires the same actor to disclose specific confidential information covered by Norm B, with no lawful restricted, anonymised, or otherwise protected method of compliance, could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Conversely, confirmation that the requesting service and supervisory-authority personnel cannot overlap would eliminate even the apparent shared-actor scenario.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger. Norm A concerns a ministerial competence to require continuation of activities; Norm B concerns confidentiality. Joint compliance remains possible, including through protected disclosure practices.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de vertrouwelijke informatie die hun bij de uitvoering van hun taken of de uitoefening van hun bevoegdheden ter kennis is gekomen, geldt voor het lid of de leden en de personeelsleden van elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zowel tijdens hun ambtstermijn als daarna het beroepsgeheim, zulks overeenkomstig Unierecht of lidstatelijk recht. Tijdens hun ambtstermijn geldt het beroepsgeheim met name voor meldingen van inbreuken op deze verordening door natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a public authority or designated organisation that is both the requesting service under Norm A and the lead supervisory authority under Norm B; the texts do not establish that these roles are held by the same actor.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap only if a transfer of recognition requiring a decision under Norm A occurs while the actor is handling a GDPR draft decision, has consulted other concerned supervisory authorities, and receives a relevant and reasoned objection within four weeks.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, when deciding to approve a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities in providing access to electronic services for a period determined by the Minister, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires the lead supervisory authority, when it rejects or considers irrelevant or unreasoned a relevant and reasoned objection, to submit the matter to the consistency mechanism referred to in Article 63.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service could continue providing reliable electronic-service access for the Minister-specified period while, if it is also the lead supervisory authority, separately submitting the disputed GDPR matter to the Article 63 consistency mechanism. The provisions regulate different acts and do not require incompatible conduct.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish that the same legal entity can simultaneously be the requesting service subject to the Minister's imposed obligation and the lead supervisory authority subject to Norm B, nor do they specify how any institutional incompatibility would be resolved. Norm A's ministerial competence is also discretionary and applies only insofar as continuity requires it.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that the same actor, for the same trigger and at the same time, must both continue the relevant activity and refrain from submitting the GDPR matter to the consistency mechanism—or that submission necessarily makes continuation legally impossible—could change the verdict. Conversely, proof that the roles are held by distinct actors would remove any practical overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger; joint compliance is possible because Norm A concerns continued electronic-service access and Norm B concerns escalation of a GDPR objection.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode
verdict.evidence_span_b: de aangelegenheid aan het in artikel 63 bedoelde coherentiemechanisme

verdict.shared_actor: Aangewezen of verzoekende dienst die elektronische diensten verleent, voor zover die dienst tevens een natuurlijke of rechtspersoon is die een inbreuk op Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 heeft begaan; de teksten bewijzen niet dat deze actoren daadwerkelijk samenvallen.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Er is mogelijk een overdracht van een erkenning waarbij continuïteit van betrouwbare elektronische dienstverlening nodig is (Norm A), terwijl dezelfde actor tevens een inbreuk op Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 heeft begaan (Norm B). Een concrete overlap van die triggers blijkt niet uit de teksten.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A geeft Onze Minister de bevoegdheid om de verzoekende dienst te verplichten haar activiteiten voor toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een bepaalde periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang te borgen.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B verplicht lidstaten om bevoegde autoriteiten de bevoegdheid te verlenen openbare mededelingen te doen waarin de identiteit van de natuurlijke of rechtspersoon die de inbreuk heeft begaan en de aard van de inbreuk worden bekendgemaakt. Dit is een bevoegdheid, geen automatische verplichting tot openbaarmaking in elk geval.
verdict.compliant_alternative: De bevoegde autoriteiten kunnen beide bevoegdheden uitoefenen: de dienst tijdelijk laten voortzetten om de continuïteit te waarborgen en, afzonderlijk, een openbare mededeling doen over de inbreuk. Indien openbaarmaking de continuïteit zou bedreigen, kan worden onderzocht of de bekendmaking wordt uitgesteld of beperkt voor zover het toepasselijke recht dat toestaat; de tekst van Norm B bevat hierover geen specifieke beperking.
verdict.unresolved_exception: Niet vastgesteld is of de verzoekende dienst onder Norm A dezelfde natuurlijke of rechtspersoon is als de inbreukmaker onder Norm B, of dat de bevoegde autoriteiten dezelfde zijn. Evenmin blijkt of openbaarmaking verenigbaar is met eventuele andere toepasselijke geheimhoudings-, gegevensbeschermings- of sectorspecifieke regels. Norm B bevat bovendien geen expliciete uitzondering voor continuïteit van dienstverlening.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: De uitkomst zou kunnen veranderen als vaststaat dat dezelfde autoriteit dezelfde actor voor exact dezelfde periode verplicht de dienstverlening voort te zetten én Norm B openbaarmaking op datzelfde moment verplicht maakt, terwijl die openbaarmaking de voortzetting juridisch of feitelijk onmogelijk maakt en geen uitstel, beperking of andere wettelijke uitzondering beschikbaar is. Op basis van de gegeven tekst is echter geen dergelijke verplichting of onverenigbaarheid aangetoond.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen wederzijds uitsluitende plichten op: Norm A verleent een bevoegdheid om continuïteit te laten voortzetten, terwijl Norm B een bevoegdheid tot openbaarmaking voorschrijft die aan lidstaten moet worden verleend. De tekst toont geen situatie waarin het ene vereist wat het andere verbiedt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen
verdict.evidence_span_b: het doen uitgaan van openbare mededelingen, met inbegrip van openbare verklaringen, waarbij de identiteit van de natuurlijke of rechtspersoon die de inbreuk heeft begaan, en de aard van de inbreuk worden bekendgemaakt

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the requesting service under Norm A if it is also a competent authority exchanging information under Norm B; the texts do not establish that this is so.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Norm A concerns a ministerial decision authorising transfer of an accreditation where continued activity is necessary to ensure continuity of reliable access to electronic services. Norm B concerns exchanges of information between competent authorities under the Regulation, where the information relates to operational or business conditions or other economic or personal matters. The provisions do not expressly establish that these circumstances coincide.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, in a transfer-authorisation decision, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities for a specified period insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires information exchanged between competent authorities under the Regulation, concerning operational or business conditions or other economic or personal matters, to be treated as confidential and subject to professional secrecy, unless the competent authority declares at the time of communication that it may be disclosed or disclosure is necessary for judicial proceedings.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service could continue the required activities while any exchanged sensitive information is kept confidential and access is restricted to authorised recipients. If disclosure is needed to implement the continuity obligation, the information could be anonymised or limited to the minimum necessary, or disclosure could be made under one of Norm B's stated exceptions.
verdict.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the requesting service is a competent authority, whether the Minister's required continuation would entail an exchange of protected information under the Regulation, and whether any proposed disclosure would fall within Norm B's declaration or judicial-proceedings exceptions.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction would require facts showing that the same actor, for the same trigger, must disclose specific information to comply with Norm A and that Norm B simultaneously forbids that disclosure without any applicable exception or confidentiality-preserving alternative. Conversely, proof that no protected information must be disclosed would make the absence of conflict clear.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties: Norm A is a competence to require continuation of activities, while Norm B regulates confidentiality of certain information exchanges. Joint compliance is possible through confidential, restricted, or anonymised handling of information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alle uitwisseling van informatie tussen de bevoegde autoriteiten krachtens deze verordening die betrekking heeft op exploitatie- of bedrijfsomstandigheden en andere economische of persoonlijke zaken, wordt als vertrouwelijk beschouwd en valt onder de vereisten van het beroepsgeheim, tenzij de bevoegde autoriteit op het moment van de mededeling verklaart dat deze informatie kan worden bekendgemaakt of de bekendmaking ervan noodzakelijk is voor gerechtelijke procedures.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a requesting service ('de verzoekende dienst') that is also an 'aanmeldende autoriteit'; the texts do not establish that these categories overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The requesting service is subject to a decision authorising transfer of recognition, and—if it is also an announcing authority—has obtained information under Article 78. The provisions do not expressly state that these triggers coincide.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, in a transfer-authorisation decision, to impose on the requesting service a duty to continue its activities providing access to electronic services for a specified period, insofar as necessary to ensure continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires announcing authorities to ensure that information obtained by them under Article 78 is treated confidentially.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The service can continue providing access while maintaining confidentiality of Article 78 information—for example, by limiting disclosure to authorised recipients, anonymising or aggregating information where operationally possible, and using a confidential fallback process for access-related communications.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify the scope of the Article 78 confidentiality obligation, any confidentiality exceptions, or whether information needed to continue reliable access must be disclosed. Norm A is a ministerial competence, not an unconditional duty imposed directly by the provision.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if the Minister's imposed continuation duty necessarily required disclosure of specific Article 78 information to persons to whom Norm B absolutely forbids disclosure, with no authorised, anonymised, restricted, or otherwise compliant means of continuing access. It would also matter whether the requesting service is in fact an announcing authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties: Norm A authorises a minister to impose a time-limited continuity duty, while Norm B requires confidentiality. The text supports simultaneous compliance through confidential handling; no unavoidable disclosure conflict is established.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: A requesting service (de verzoekende dienst) that may also be a notified body (aangemelde instantie) or its subsidiary/subcontractor, subject to the respective provisions
verdict.shared_circumstance: A transfer/continuation context in which the service performs activities relating to access to electronic services and, potentially, activities are performed through a subcontractor or subsidiary with the provider's consent
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, where necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its access-related activities for a specified period.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires notified bodies to make a list of their subsidiaries public; activities may be performed by a subcontractor or subsidiary only with the provider's consent.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The provisions do not establish that the requesting service is a notified body, subsidiary, or subcontractor, nor do they specify how the transfer decision interacts with the provider-consent requirement. Those factual and procedural links remain unresolved.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose different, potentially cumulative requirements: a ministerial power to require temporary continuation and a disclosure/consent regime for subcontracting or subsidiaries. Neither rule forbids compliance with the other, and no mutually exclusive duty is shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Activiteiten mogen uitsluitend met instemming van de aanbieder door een onderaannemer of dochteronderneming worden uitgevoerd. Aangemelde instanties maken een lijst van hun dochterondernemingen openbaar.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially a requesting service under BWBR0048156 art. 14 and a notifying authority under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 art. 45, but the provisions do not establish that these are the same actor or that a requesting service is a notifying authority.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap if the same public body is both the requesting service seeking transfer of an accreditation and a notifying authority that has obtained information under Article 78, during a period in which continued electronic-service access activities are required or exercised.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, upon authorising a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities concerning enterprises' and legal persons' access to electronic services for a specified period, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained by them in accordance with Article 78 is treated confidentially.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service can continue providing access to electronic services while restricting disclosure of Article 78 information to authorised recipients, applying confidentiality safeguards and anonymisation or redaction where information must be used operationally. Nothing in Norm A requires disclosure of confidential information, and Norm B does not prohibit continuing the relevant activities.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not specify whether the requesting service is also a notifying authority, what information must be kept confidential under Article 78, or whether continuity of access would in a particular case require disclosure of that information. Any applicable disclosure exception or legally required disclosure mechanism is unresolved.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A fact showing that compliance with the Minister's continuity order necessarily requires the same actor to disclose information that Article 45 requires it to keep confidential—and that no authorised, anonymised, restricted, or otherwise lawful disclosure route exists—could change the verdict to CONTRADICTION. Conversely, proof that the actors cannot be the same would eliminate even the potential overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not mutually exclusive on the supplied text: continuing electronic-service access can coexist with confidential treatment of obtained Article 78 information, including through restricted disclosure or safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially an organisation that is both the requesting service under BWBR0048156 and a national competent authority under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; the texts do not establish that these categories necessarily overlap.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The overlap would arise if that actor requests and receives authorisation to transfer an accreditation, while also performing its tasks as a national competent authority. Norm A additionally requires that continuation be necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access to electronic services; Norm B applies when the authority performs its tasks.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, in the decision authorising transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities concerning access to electronic services for a specified period, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B obliges national competent authorities, when performing their tasks, to comply with the confidentiality obligations laid down in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service can continue providing access while complying with Article 78 confidentiality duties—for example, by continuing the service with restricted disclosure, access controls, anonymisation or redaction of protected information, and a limited continuation period. Nothing in Norm A requires disclosure of confidential information.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The supplied text does not specify the content or scope of Article 78, nor whether the requesting service is in fact a national competent authority or whether any particular continuation activity would necessarily require a prohibited disclosure. Those issues could affect practical compliance but do not establish a contradiction on this text.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible if Article 78 expressly prohibited an act that continuation under Norm A necessarily required, with no possibility of restricted disclosure, anonymisation, or another compliant method; alternatively, proof that the actor categories cannot overlap would eliminate even a potential shared application.
verdict.criterion_fired: The rules impose different, jointly satisfiable requirements: Norm A concerns a ministerial competence to require temporary continuation, while Norm B concerns confidentiality compliance. The provisions do not require and forbid the same act.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij de uitvoering van hun taken voldoen de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten aan de in artikel 78 vastgelegde vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: Potentially the requesting service under Norm A and the public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) under Norm B, but the provisions do not establish that these are the same actor.
verdict.shared_circumstance: The provisions could overlap if the requesting service is also an Article 77(1) public authority or body, receives or handles information or documentation obtained under Article 77, and is subject to a transfer-approval decision requiring continued electronic-service access activities.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, when approving a transfer, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities concerning enterprises' and legal persons' access to electronic services for a specified period, insofar as necessary to safeguard continuity of reliable access.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B requires information or documentation obtained under Article 77 by the authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) to be processed in accordance with the confidentiality obligations described in Article 78.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service could continue the required access activities while processing any Article 77 information in accordance with Article 78—for example, by restricting disclosure and access to authorised persons, maintaining confidentiality safeguards, and using only the information necessary for continuity. Nothing in the quoted provisions requires disclosure of confidential information as part of continued service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The text does not provide Article 78's confidentiality obligations, identify the Article 77(1) authorities or bodies, or specify whether the requesting service is among them. It is therefore unresolved whether any concrete operational measure required by Norm A would conflict with a particular Article 78 restriction.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become possible if Article 78 expressly prohibited a specific act that Norm A necessarily required the requesting service to perform, or if the requesting service were required to disclose Article 77 information in a manner that Article 78 forbids. Conversely, confirmation that the requesting service is not an Article 77(1) authority or does not process Article 77 information would eliminate the overlap.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions impose different duties and do not, on the quoted text, require mutually exclusive conduct: Norm A concerns continued electronic-service activities under a ministerial transfer decision, while Norm B concerns confidential processing of information obtained under Article 77. Joint compliance remains plausible through confidentiality-preserving processing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verzoekende dienst de verplichting opleggen zijn activiteiten in de toegang van ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang door ondernemingen en rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_actor: No clearly established shared actor. Norm A concerns the requesting service involved in transferring an electronic-service recognition; Norm B concerns national public authorities or bodies supervising or enforcing fundamental-rights obligations concerning certain high-risk AI systems.
verdict.shared_circumstance: Both may concern public-sector electronic or AI-related services and may arise during regulatory oversight or continuity of service, but the provisions do not establish the same legal trigger or subject matter.
verdict.requirement_a: Norm A gives the Minister competence, when authorising a transfer of recognition, to impose on the requesting service an obligation to continue its activities for a specified period insofar as necessary to ensure continuity of reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.requirement_b: Norm B gives qualifying national authorities or bodies competence to request and inspect documentation prepared or maintained under the AI Regulation, in an accessible language and format, when access is necessary for effective exercise of their mandate within their jurisdiction; the authority must notify the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.compliant_alternative: The requesting service could continue providing access as required by the Minister while separately supplying the requested AI documentation to the competent authority in the required accessible form, subject to the authority's jurisdiction and necessity condition. Nothing in either provision requires withholding the documentation or discontinuing the service.
verdict.unresolved_exception: The texts do not establish whether the requesting service is also the entity holding the documentation, whether the service concerns a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, or whether confidentiality, data-protection, or other sector-specific restrictions affect inspection. Those issues may govern implementation but do not create a demonstrated contradiction here.
verdict.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction would require a specific additional rule or fact showing that compliance with the Minister's continuity obligation necessarily forbids the requesting service from providing the documentation, or that the authority's inspection order necessarily requires suspending or ceasing the activities that Norm A requires it to continue. It would also matter if the same actor and identical trigger were legally established and the duties were mutually exclusive.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger.
